sentences.zh: 崔縱，字元矩，撫州臨川人。

translations.literal: Cui Zong, styled Yuanju, was a native of Linchuan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zong, styled Yuanju, was from Linchuan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 登政和五年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Zhenghe reign.

sentences.zh: 曆確山主簿、仙居丞，累遷承議郎、幹辦審計司。

translations.literal: He served as Recorder of Queshan and Assistant Magistrate of Xianju, and was promoted repeatedly to Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and Handler in the Audit Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder of Queshan and assistant magistrate of Xianju, then rose through successive posts to Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and handler in the Audit Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二帝北行，高宗將遣使通問，廷臣以前使者相繼受係，莫肯往。

translations.literal: When the two emperors were taken north, Emperor Gaozong was about to send envoys to inquire after them; court officials, seeing that previous envoys had been detained one after another, none would go.
translations.idiomatic: After the two emperors were marched north, Emperor Gaozong prepared to send envoys to inquire after them, but no court official would go—earlier envoys had been detained one after another.

sentences.zh: 縱毅然請行，乃授朝請大夫、右文殿修撰、試工部尚書以行。

translations.literal: Zong resolutely volunteered to go and was therefore appointed Gentleman for Court Audience, Compiler at the Hall of Literary Glory on the Right, and Acting Minister of Works for the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Zong volunteered resolutely to go and was appointed Gentleman for Court Audience, compiler at the Hall of Literary Glory on the Right, and acting Minister of Works for the journey.

sentences.zh: 比至，首以大義責金人，請還二帝，又三遺之書。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he first rebuked the Jurchens on grounds of righteousness, demanded the return of the two emperors, and sent them three further letters.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he first rebuked the Jurchens in the name of righteousness, demanded the return of the two emperors, and sent them three more letters besides.

sentences.zh: 金人怒，徙之窮荒，縱不少屈。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were enraged and exiled him to the wilderness; Zong would not yield in the least.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens were furious and banished him to the wilds, but Zong would not bend.

sentences.zh: 久之，金人許南使自陳而聽其還，縱以王事未畢不忍言。

translations.literal: After a long time the Jurchens allowed southern envoys to petition on their own behalf and be permitted to return; Zong, because his royal mission was unfinished, could not bring himself to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: In time the Jurchens allowed southern envoys to plead their own case and go home, but Zong, his royal mission still unfinished, could not bring himself to ask.

sentences.zh: 又以官爵誘之，縱以恚恨成疾，竟握節以死。

translations.literal: They also tempted him with office and rank; Zong, full of indignation and resentment, fell ill and in the end died clutching his credentials.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to lure him with office and rank as well; consumed by indignation, he fell ill and died still clutching his credentials.

sentences.zh: 洪皓、張邵還，遂歸縱之骨。

translations.literal: When Hong Hao and Zhang Shao returned, Zong's bones were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Hao and Zhang Shao came home, Zong's remains were returned with them.

sentences.zh: 詔以兄子延年為後。

translations.literal: An edict made his elder brother's son Yannian his heir.
translations.idiomatic: The court decreed that his elder brother's son Yannian would succeed him.

sentences.zh: 吳安國字鎮卿，處州人。

translations.literal: Wu Anguo, styled Zhenqing, was a native of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Anguo, styled Zhenqing, was from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太學進士，累官遷考功郎官。

translations.literal: A Metropolitan University jinshi, he rose through offices to become an Investigator in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A Metropolitan University jinshi, he rose through successive posts to investigator in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以太常少卿使金，值金人渝盟，拘留脅服之，安國毅然正色曰：“我首可得，我節不可奪，惟知竭誠死王事，王命烏敢辱？

translations.literal: As Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was sent as envoy to the Jin; when the Jurchens broke the treaty and detained him, trying to force his submission, Anguo said with stern resolve and an unflinching countenance: "You may have my head, but you cannot take my integrity. I know only to exhaust my loyalty and die in the king's service—how would I dare disgrace the royal command?
translations.idiomatic: Sent to the Jin as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he arrived just as the Jurchens broke the treaty and held him, trying to force his submission. Anguo faced them squarely and said: "You may take my head, but you cannot break my integrity. I know only to give my all and die in the king's service—how would I dare dishonor the royal command?

sentences.zh: ”金人不敢犯，遣還。

translations.literal: " The Jurchens did not dare harm him and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jurchens did not dare touch him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 後知袁州，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as prefect of Yuanzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Yuanzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 林衝之，字和叔，興化軍莆田人。

translations.literal: Lin Chongzhi, styled Heshu, was a native of Putian in the Xinghua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Chongzhi, styled Heshu, was from Putian in the Xinghua Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元符三年進士，曆御史台檢法官、大宗正丞，都官、金部郎，滯省寺者十年。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Yuanfu, he served as Investigating Censor in the Censorate, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and Director in the Ministries of Justice and Revenue, remaining in central offices for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Yuanfu and served as investigating censor, assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and director in the ministries of Justice and Revenue, spending ten years in the central bureaucracy without advancement.

sentences.zh: 出守臨江、南康。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Linjiang and Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out to govern Linjiang and Nankang.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，召為主客郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era he was summoned to be Director in the Ministry of Rites for Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang crisis he was recalled to serve as director in the Ministry of Rites for Receptions.

sentences.zh: 金人再來侵，詔副中書侍郎陳過庭使金，同被拘執。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded again, an edict appointed him deputy to Vice Director of the Secretariat Chen Guoting on a mission to the Jin; both were detained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded again, he was ordered to accompany Vice Director of the Secretariat Chen Guoting as envoy to the Jin; both were taken captive.

sentences.zh: 初猶給乳酪，迨宇文虛中受其命，金人亦以是邀之，衝之奮厲見詞色，金人怒，徙之奉聖州。

translations.literal: At first they still supplied him with dairy foods; but when Yuwen Xuzhong accepted their appointment, the Jurchens made the same offer to Chongzhi—who responded with fierce indignation plain in word and face. The Jurchens were enraged and transferred him to Fengsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At first they still gave him dairy foods, but after Yuwen Xuzhong accepted office under them the Jurchens made the same offer to Chongzhi. He answered with blazing defiance in both word and bearing. The Jurchens were furious and moved him to Fengsheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既二年，過庭卒，金人逼衝之仕偽齊，不屈；

translations.literal: After two years Guoting died; the Jurchens pressed Chongzhi to serve the puppet Qi state, but he would not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Guoting died. The Jurchens pressed Chongzhi to serve the puppet Qi regime, but he refused;

sentences.zh: 徙上京，又不屈；

translations.literal: he was moved to the Supreme Capital and again would not submit;
translations.idiomatic: they moved him to the Supreme Capital and again he would not yield;

sentences.zh: 置顯州極北沍寒之地，幽佛寺十餘年。

translations.literal: he was placed in Xianzhou, the bitterly cold northern extremity, and kept in seclusion at a Buddhist temple for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: finally they confined him in Xianzhou, the bitterly cold far north, where he lived in seclusion at a Buddhist temple for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 漸便飲茹，以義命自安，髭發還黑。

translations.literal: Gradually he grew accustomed to his diet of coarse fare, found peace in accepting fate by righteousness, and his beard and hair turned black again.
translations.idiomatic: In time he adapted to his plain diet, found peace in accepting his lot through righteousness, and even his beard and hair turned black again.

sentences.zh: 病亟，語同難者曰：“某年七十二，持忠入地無恨，所恨者國仇未復耳。

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical he told his fellow sufferers: "I am seventy-two years old; to take my loyalty into the grave without regret is enough—the only regret is that the national enemy has not yet been avenged.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened he told his fellow captives: "I am seventy-two. I can go to my grave loyal and without regret. My only regret is that the national enemy has not yet been avenged.

sentences.zh: ”南向一慟而絕。

translations.literal: " He gave one great lament facing south and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He cried out once toward the south and died.

sentences.zh: 僧窆之寺隅。

translations.literal: Monks buried him in a corner of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The monks buried him in a corner of the temple grounds.

sentences.zh: 洪皓還朝以聞，詔與二子官。

translations.literal: When Hong Hao returned to court and reported this, an edict granted offices to his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Hao returned and reported his death, the court granted offices to both his sons.

sentences.zh: 子鬱，從子震、霆。

translations.literal: His son was Yu; his nephews were Zhen and Ting.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu; his nephews were Zhen and Ting.

sentences.zh: 鬱字襲休，宣和三年進士，再調福建茶司幹官。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Xiuxiu, was a jinshi of the third year of Xuanhe and was twice assigned as handler in the Fujian Tea Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Xiuxiu, passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Xuanhe and twice served as handler in the Fujian Tea Commission.

sentences.zh: 建州勤王卒自京師還，求卸甲錢，郡守逃匿，卒鼓噪取庫兵為亂，殺轉運使毛奎、轉運判官曾仔、主管文字沈升。

translations.literal: When troops from Jianzhou who had marched to the capital's relief returned from the capital demanding demobilization pay, the prefect fled and hid; the soldiers raised a clamor, seized weapons from the arsenal, and rebelled, killing Transport Commissioner Mao Kui, Transport Vice Commissioner Zeng Zai, and chief clerk Shen Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianzhou troops who had marched to relieve the capital returned demanding demobilization pay, the prefect fled. The soldiers rioted, seized arms from the arsenal, and killed Transport Commissioner Mao Kui, transport vice commissioner Zeng Zai, and chief clerk Shen Sheng.

sentences.zh: 鬱聞變急入諭卒，遇害。

translations.literal: Yu, hearing of the disturbance, rushed in to reason with the soldiers and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, hearing of the riot, rushed in to reason with the troops and was killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔各與一子官。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict granted each of them an office for one son.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, each man was granted an office for one son.

sentences.zh: 霆字時隱，政和五年進士，敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: Ting, styled Shiyin, was a jinshi of the fifth year of Zhenghe and a revising officer in the Statutes Office.
translations.idiomatic: Ting, styled Shiyin, was a jinshi of the fifth year of Zhenghe and served as a revising officer in the Statutes Office.

sentences.zh: 詆紹興和議，謂不宜置二帝萬里外不通問，即掛冠出都門，權臣大恚怒，亦廢放以死，莆人稱為“忠義林氏”。

translations.literal: He denounced the Shaoxing peace agreement, saying it was wrong to leave the two emperors ten thousand li away with no communication; he immediately resigned his cap and left the capital. The powerful minister was greatly enraged and had him dismissed and banished until death. The people of Putian called them "the loyal Lin clan."
translations.idiomatic: He condemned the Shaoxing peace treaty, arguing that the two emperors should not be left ten thousand li away with no word from home. He resigned at once and left the capital. The powerful minister was furious and had him dismissed and exiled until he died. The people of Putian called them "the loyal Lin family."

sentences.zh: 寶慶三年，即其所居立祠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing a shrine was erected at his former residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing a shrine was built at his former home.

sentences.zh: 寶祐中，又給田百畝，使備祭享以勸忠義雲。

translations.literal: During the Baoyou era another hundred mu of land was granted so that sacrifices could be maintained, to encourage loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoyou era the court granted another hundred mu of land for sacrificial upkeep, to encourage loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 滕茂實字秀穎，杭州臨安人。

translations.literal: Teng Maoshi, styled Xiuying, was a native of Lin'an in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Maoshi, styled Xiuying, was from Lin'an in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 政和八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eighth year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，以工部員外郎假工部侍郎，副路允迪出使，為金人所留。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, as Director in the Ministry of Works he was given the acting rank of Vice Minister of Works and served as deputy to Lu Yundi on an embassy; he was detained by the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he served as director in the Ministry of Works with acting rank of vice minister and accompanied Lu Yundi as deputy envoy; the Jurchens detained him.

sentences.zh: 時茂實兄陶通判代州，已先降金。

translations.literal: At that time Maoshi's elder brother Tao, assistant prefect of Daizhou, had already surrendered to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: By then Maoshi's elder brother Tao, assistant prefect of Daizhou, had already surrendered to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 粘罕素聞茂實名，乃遷之代州，又自京師取其弟華實同居，以慰其意。

translations.literal: Nianhan had long heard of Maoshi's reputation and therefore transferred him to Daizhou; he also brought his younger brother Huashi from the capital to live with him, to comfort his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan had long known Maoshi's reputation and moved him to Daizhou, then brought his younger brother Huashi from the capital to live with him, hoping to console him.

sentences.zh: 欽宗自離都城，舊臣無敢候問起居者。

translations.literal: From the time Emperor Qinzong left the capital, none of his former ministers dared inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Qinzong left the capital, none of his former ministers dared inquire after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 茂實聞欽宗將至，即自為哀詞，且篆“宋工部侍郎滕茂實墓”九字，取奉使黃幡裹之，以授其友人朔寧府司理董詵。

translations.literal: When Maoshi heard that Qinzong was coming, he at once composed his own elegy and carved in seal script the nine characters "Tomb of Teng Maoshi, Vice Minister of Works of Song," wrapped them in the yellow banner of his embassy credentials, and gave them to his friend Dong Shen, magistrate of Shuoning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Qinzong was approaching, Maoshi wrote his own elegy, carved in seal script the nine characters "Tomb of Teng Maoshi, Vice Minister of Works of Song," wrapped them in the yellow banner of his embassy credentials, and entrusted them to his friend Dong Shen, magistrate of Shuoning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 欽宗及郊，茂實具冠幘迎謁，拜伏號泣。

translations.literal: When Qinzong performed the suburban sacrifice, Maoshi put on cap and headcloth to meet and pay respects, prostrating himself and wailing.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong performed the suburban sacrifice, Maoshi dressed in full cap and headcloth to greet him, prostrating himself and weeping aloud.

sentences.zh: 金人諭之曰：“國破主遷，所以留公，蓋將大用。

translations.literal: The Jurchens admonished him: "The state is broken and the ruler removed—that is why we have kept you here; we intend to employ you greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens told him: "The state is fallen and the ruler displaced—that is why we kept you. We mean to give you great office.

sentences.zh: ”迫令易服，茂實力拒不從，見者墮淚。

translations.literal: " They forced him to change his dress; Maoshi strenuously refused, and those who saw it shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: " They forced him to change his dress, but Maoshi resisted with all his strength; those who witnessed it wept.

sentences.zh: 茂實請從舊主俱行，金人不許，憂憤成疾，卒雲中。

translations.literal: Maoshi asked to accompany his former sovereign, but the Jurchens would not permit it; grief and indignation brought on illness, and he died at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Maoshi asked to follow his former sovereign, but the Jurchens refused. Grief and rage brought on illness, and he died at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 詵拔歸，錄所為哀詞言於張浚，浚以詵為陝西轉運判官，上其事。

translations.literal: Shen escaped and returned, recorded the elegy Maoshi had written, and reported it to Zhang Jun; Jun appointed Shen transport vice commissioner of Shaanxi and submitted the account to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shen made his way home, copied down the elegy, and reported it to Zhang Jun, who appointed Shen transport vice commissioner of Shaanxi and submitted the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，贈龍圖閣直學士，官其家三人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing he was posthumously made a direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and three members of his family were granted office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing he was posthumously made direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and three members of his family received offices.

sentences.zh: 魏行可，建州建安人。

translations.literal: Wei Xingke was a native of Jian'an in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xingke was from Jian'an in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，以太學生應募奉使，補右奉議郎，假朝奉大夫、尚書禮部侍郎，充河北金人軍前通問使，仍命兼河北、京畿撫諭使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan, as a Metropolitan University student he volunteered for an embassy and was made Right Gentleman for Discussion of Policy, given the acting rank of Grand Master for Court Audience and Vice Minister of Rites, and appointed envoy to communicate with the Jurchen armies in Hebei; he was also ordered to serve concurrently as pacification commissioner for Hebei and the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan he volunteered from the Metropolitan University for an embassy and was made Right Gentleman for Discussion of Policy with acting rank of Grand Master for Court Audience and Vice Minister of Rites, appointed envoy to communicate with the Jurchen armies in Hebei and concurrently pacification commissioner for Hebei and the capital region.

sentences.zh: 時河北紅巾賊甚眾，行可始懼為所攻，既而見使旌，皆引去。

translations.literal: At that time red-turban bandits were numerous in Hebei; Xingke at first feared attack, but when they saw the embassy banners they all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Red-turban bandits were thick in Hebei at the time. Xingke first feared they would attack him, but when they saw the embassy banners they all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 行可渡河見金人於澶淵，金人知其布衣借官，待之甚薄，因留不遣。

translations.literal: Xingke crossed the river and met the Jurchens at Chanyuan; knowing he was a commoner given borrowed rank, they treated him very poorly and detained him without release.
translations.idiomatic: Xingke crossed the river and met the Jurchens at Chanyuan. Knowing he was a commoner wearing borrowed rank, they treated him coldly and kept him without release.

sentences.zh: 行可嚐貽書金人，警以“不戢自焚”之禍：“大國舉中原與劉豫，劉氏何德？

translations.literal: Xingke once sent the Jurchens a letter warning them of the disaster of "those who do not restrain themselves burn themselves": "The great state has given the Central Plains to Liu Yu—what virtue has the Liu house?
translations.idiomatic: Xingke once wrote the Jurchens warning of the disaster of those who cannot restrain themselves: "Your great state has handed the Central Plains to Liu Yu—what virtue has the Liu house shown?

sentences.zh: 趙氏何罪？

translations.literal: What crime has the Zhao house committed?
translations.idiomatic: What crime has the Zhao house committed?

sentences.zh: 若亟以還趙氏，賢於奉劉氏萬萬也。

translations.literal: If you quickly return it to the Zhao house, that would be ten thousand times better than supporting the Liu house.
translations.idiomatic: If you return it to the Zhao house at once, that would be infinitely better than backing the Liu house.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 十三年，張邵來歸，言行可執節沒於王事，行可父通直郎伯能亦訴於朝，遂贈朝奉郎、秘閣修撰，先已官其二子一弟，至是，復官其一孫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhang Shao returned and reported that Xingke had upheld his credentials and died in the king's service; Xingke's father, Regular Attendant Boleng, also petitioned the court, and he was posthumously made Grand Master for Court Audience and Compiler at the Secretariat Archive. Offices had already been granted to two sons and one younger brother; now one grandson received office as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhang Shao came home and reported that Xingke had died upholding his credentials in the king's service. Xingke's father Boleng, a regular attendant, also petitioned the court, and Xingke was posthumously made Grand Master for Court Audience and compiler at the Secretariat Archive. Two sons and a younger brother had already received offices; now a grandson did as well.

sentences.zh: 行可之使也，吳人郭元邁以上舍應募，補右武大夫、和州團練使為之副，不肯髡發換官，亦卒於北焉。

translations.literal: On Xingke's mission, Guo Yuanmai of Wu, a senior student who had volunteered, was made Right Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and regimental commander of Hezhou as his deputy; he refused to shave his head and change office, and also died in the north.
translations.idiomatic: On Xingke's mission, Guo Yuanmai of Wu, a senior Metropolitan University student who volunteered, served as his deputy with rank of Right Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and regimental commander of Hezhou. He refused to shave his head and accept office under the Jurchens, and likewise died in the north.

sentences.zh: 閻進，隸宣武。

translations.literal: Yan Jin was attached to the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jin served in the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，遣使通問，進從行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan envoys were sent to communicate; Jin accompanied the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era envoys were sent to communicate with the north, and Jin went with them.

sentences.zh: 既至雲中府，金人拘留使者散處之，進亡去。

translations.literal: When they reached Yunzhong Prefecture the Jurchens detained the envoys and dispersed them; Jin fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhong Prefecture the Jurchens detained the envoys and scattered them; Jin escaped.

sentences.zh: 追還，留守高慶裔問：“何為亡？

translations.literal: Pursued and brought back, the garrison commander Gao Qingyi asked: "Why did you flee?
translations.idiomatic: Recaptured, Garrison Commander Gao Qingyi asked: "Why did you run away?

sentences.zh: ”進曰：“思大宋爾。

translations.literal: " Jin said: "Because I long for Great Song.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin said: "Because I long for the Great Song.

sentences.zh: ”又問：“郎主待汝有恩，汝亡何故？

translations.literal: " He asked again: "Our sovereign has shown you favor—why flee?
translations.idiomatic: " He asked again: "Our sovereign has treated you kindly—why flee?

sentences.zh: ”進曰：“錦衣玉食亦不戀也。

translations.literal: " Jin said: "Even brocade robes and jade fare I do not desire.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin said: "I would not cling even to brocade robes and jade fare.

sentences.zh: ”慶裔義而釋之。

translations.literal: " Qingyi, moved by righteousness, released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Moved by his integrity, Qingyi let him go.

sentences.zh: 凡三亡乃見殺。

translations.literal: After three escapes he was finally killed.
translations.idiomatic: After three escapes he was finally put to death.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，進謂行刑者：“吾南向受刃，南則我皇帝行在也。

translations.literal: At the execution Jin said to the executioner: "Let me receive the blade facing south—for south is where my emperor's traveling court lies.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Jin told the executioner: "Let me take the blade facing south—for south is where my emperor's traveling court lies.

sentences.zh: ”行刑者曳其臂令麵北，進踴身直起，盤旋數四，卒南鄉就死。

translations.literal: " The executioner dragged his arm to make him face north; Jin leaped upright, spun around several times, and finally died facing south.
translations.idiomatic: " The executioner dragged his arm to turn him north. Jin sprang upright, spun around several times, and at last died facing south.

sentences.zh: 進武校尉朱績亦從之，分在粘罕所。

translations.literal: Military Instructor Zhu Ji of the Palace Guard also accompanied the mission and was assigned to Nianhan's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard military instructor Zhu Ji also went on the mission and was placed in Nianhan's camp.

sentences.zh: 績見粘罕數日，遽求妻室。

translations.literal: After several days with Nianhan, Ji suddenly asked for a wife.
translations.idiomatic: After a few days with Nianhan, Ji suddenly asked for a wife.

sentences.zh: 粘罕喜，令擇所虜內人妻之，績取最醜者，人莫諭其意。

translations.literal: Nianhan was pleased and ordered him to choose from captive women; Ji took the ugliest, and no one understood his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan was pleased and let him choose from captive women. Ji took the ugliest one, and no one understood why.

sentences.zh: 不半月亡去，追之還，粘罕大怒，績含笑死梃下。

translations.literal: Within half a month he fled; pursued and brought back, Nianhan was furious, but Ji died smiling under the clubs.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a month he fled. Recaptured, he enraged Nianhan—but Ji died smiling under the clubs.

sentences.zh: 蓋績求妻者，所以固粘罕也。

translations.literal: It turned out Ji had sought a wife in order to reassure Nianhan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had asked for a wife only to put Nianhan at ease.

sentences.zh: 趙師檟以罪拘管西外宗正司，福建提刑王夢龍以智勇可用，屬製軍器。

translations.literal: Zhao Shijiao was detained in the Outer Western Directorate of the Imperial Clan on a charge; Fujian transport judicial commissioner Wang Menglong, finding him intelligent and brave, put him in charge of making weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shijiao was held in the Outer Western Directorate of the Imperial Clan on a charge. Fujian transport judicial commissioner Wang Menglong, judging him clever and brave, put him in charge of arms production.

sentences.zh: 會寇逼尤溪，令師檟統卒數百往戍。

translations.literal: When bandits threatened Youxi, Shijiao was ordered to command several hundred soldiers to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits pressed on Youxi, he was ordered to lead several hundred men to garrison the county.

sentences.zh: 既行，大書於旗曰：“不與賊俱生。

translations.literal: Before departing he wrote large characters on his banner: "I will not live together with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched he wrote large characters on his banner: "I will not live while the bandits live.

sentences.zh: ”人皆壯之。

translations.literal: " All admired him.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone took heart from him.

sentences.zh: 賊兵至，師檟迎敵於林嶺，身為先鋒。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived, Shijiao met them at Linling, taking the vanguard himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came, Shijiao met them at Linling and led the charge himself.

sentences.zh: 戰十餘合，賊至益眾，師檟所乘馬適陷田中，賊斷其左臂，師檟以右手拔背刀斬七級。

translations.literal: After more than ten exchanges the bandits grew more numerous; Shijiao's horse happened to sink in a field and bandits severed his left arm; with his right hand he drew the sword on his back and beheaded seven men.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten clashes the bandits swelled in number. Shijiao's horse sank in a field and bandits cut off his left arm; with his right hand he drew the sword on his back and took seven heads.

sentences.zh: 力盡，部曲欲引遁，師檟仰天大呼曰：“師檟報國死於此矣。

translations.literal: When his strength was spent, his troops wanted to retreat; Shijiao looked to heaven and shouted: "Shijiao repays the state by dying here!
translations.idiomatic: Spent, his men wanted to pull back. Shijiao looked to heaven and cried: "Shijiao dies here repaying the state!

sentences.zh: ”遂沒焉。

translations.literal: " And so he perished.
translations.idiomatic: " And there he fell.

sentences.zh: 尤溪之民為之立廟戰處。

translations.literal: The people of Youxi built a temple for him at the battle site.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Youxi built him a temple on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 樞密王野請加褒贈，乃贈武節郎，與一子恩澤。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Ye requested posthumous honors; he was made Military Festival Gentleman and one son received imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Ye asked for posthumous honors; Shijiao was made Military Festival Gentleman and one son received imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 易青者，為都督行府摧鋒軍效用。

translations.literal: Yi Qing served as a merit soldier in the Vanguard Army of the Grand Marshal's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qing was a merit soldier in the Vanguard Army under the Grand Marshal's field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，廣東賊曾袞本軍士也，已受招復叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Guangdong bandit Zeng Gun had been a soldier in the army, had accepted amnesty, and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong bandit Zeng Gun had once been a regular soldier, accepted amnesty, then rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年十月，經略使連南夫與摧鋒軍統製韓京會於惠州，督諸兵討之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Shaoxing, Pacification Commissioner Lian Nanfu and Vanguard Army commander Han Jing met at Huizhou and directed the troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Shaoxing, Pacification Commissioner Lian Nanfu and Vanguard commander Han Jing assembled at Huizhou to lead the campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 京募敢死士七十三人夜劫袞營，青在行中，為所執。

translations.literal: Jing recruited seventy-three dare-to-die men for a night raid on Gun's camp; Qing was among them and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jing recruited seventy-three dare-to-die men for a night raid on Gun's camp. Qing went with them and was taken.

sentences.zh: 賊驅至後軍趙續砦外，謂續曰：“汝大軍為我所擒者甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits drove him to outside Rear Army Commander Zhao Xu's fort and said to Xu: "Your great army has many men captured by us.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits brought him to outside Rear Army Commander Zhao Xu's fort and told Xu: "We have captured many of your great army's men.

sentences.zh: ”青大呼曰：“勿信，所擒者我爾。

translations.literal: " Qing shouted: "Do not believe them—the one captured is only me.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing shouted: "Don't believe them—the only captive is me.

sentences.zh: ”賊又言：“吾不汝殺，第令經略持黃榜來招安。

translations.literal: " The bandits said again: "We will not kill you—only have the pacification commissioner bring a yellow placard to offer amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits added: "We won't kill you—just have the pacification commissioner bring a yellow placard offering amnesty.

sentences.zh: ”青又呼曰：“勿聽，任賊殺我，我惟以一死報國。

translations.literal: " Qing shouted again: "Do not listen—let the bandits kill me; I have only this one death to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing cried again: "Don't listen! Let the bandits kill me—I have only this one death to give the state.

sentences.zh: ”賊怒焚之，青死，罵不絕口。

translations.literal: " The bandits in rage burned him; Qing died cursing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits burned him in fury. Qing died still cursing without stop.

sentences.zh: 青無妻子。

translations.literal: Qing had no wife or children.
translations.idiomatic: Qing left no wife or children.

sentences.zh: 事聞，特贈保義郎、閣門祗候，官為薦祭焉。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was specially posthumously made Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and Palace Gate Attendant, and the state provided sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was specially posthumously made Gentleman for Preserving Righteousness and Palace Gate Attendant, and the state provided for his sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 胡斌，為殿前司將官。

translations.literal: Hu Bin was a general officer of the Palace Command.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bin was a general officer in the Palace Command.

sentences.zh: 童德興提禁旅戍邵武，江、閩寇作，知邵武有備，未敢犯。

translations.literal: Tong Dexing led the imperial guard to garrison Shaowu; when bandits rose in Jiangxi and Fujian, knowing Shaowu was prepared, they did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Dexing led the imperial guard to garrison Shaowu. When bandits rose in Jiangxi and Fujian, they knew Shaowu was ready and did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 會招捕司檄德興稟議，獨留斌將弱卒數百留城中。

translations.literal: When the Pacification Office summoned Dexing for consultation, only Bin was left with several hundred weak soldiers in the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pacification Office summoned Dexing for consultation, only Bin remained in the city with a few hundred weak troops.

sentences.zh: 紹定三年閏月己卯，盜眾大至，他將士皆遁，獨斌奮身迎戰，所格殺甚眾。

translations.literal: On the jimao day of the intercalary month in the third year of Shaoding, bandits came in force; other officers and soldiers all fled, but Bin alone threw himself into battle and killed many in close combat.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day of the intercalary month in the third year of Shaoding, bandits swarmed in. Other officers and men fled; Bin alone threw himself into the fight and killed many at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 賊益生兵，官軍所存僅數十人，或告以眾寡不敵，盍避之！

translations.literal: The bandits sent more troops; only several dozen government soldiers remained, and some told him the odds were hopeless and he should withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits brought up more men. Only a few dozen government troops remained. Some urged him that the odds were hopeless and he should withdraw.

sentences.zh: 斌曰：“郡民死者以萬計，賴生者數千人由東門而出，我不綴其勢，使得脫走，則賊躡其後，無噍類矣。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Tens of thousands in the prefecture have died; several thousand survivors depend on getting out through the east gate. If I do not check the bandits' momentum and let them escape, the bandits will pursue and none will be left alive.
translations.idiomatic: Bin said: "Tens of thousands in this prefecture are dead. Several thousand survivors are counting on the east gate. If I don't hold the bandits back and let those people escape, the bandits will run them down and leave no one alive.

sentences.zh: ”遂巷戰，大呼曰：“我死救百姓。

translations.literal: " He fought in the alleys, shouting: "I die to save the people.
translations.idiomatic: " He fought street by street, shouting: "I die to save the people!

sentences.zh: ”兵盡矢窮，卒遇害，其屍僵立，移時始仆。

translations.literal: " His men and arrows were exhausted; he was finally killed. His corpse stood rigid and only fell after some time.
translations.idiomatic: " His men and arrows gave out. He was killed at last. His body stood rigid and did not fall for some time.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈武節大夫，錄其後一人。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Grand Master of Military Festival and one descendant was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Grand Master of Military Festival and one descendant received office.

sentences.zh: 樞密院編修官王野言邵武民即斌戰地立廟，請就以“武節”為廟額，從之。

translations.literal: Compilation reviser Wang Ye of the Bureau of Military Affairs reported that the people of Shaowu had built a temple at Bin's battle site and requested the plaque "Military Festival"; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation reviser Wang Ye reported that the people of Shaowu had built a temple on Bin's battlefield and asked that its plaque read Military Festival; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 範旺，南劍州順昌縣巡檢司軍校也。

translations.literal: Fan Wang was a military corporal in the Shunchang County patrol office of Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wang was a corporal in the Shunchang County patrol office of Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，順昌盜俞勝等作亂，官吏皆散，土軍陳望素樂禍，與射士張袞謀舉砦應之，旺叱之曰：“吾等父母妻子皆受國家廩食以活，今力不能討，反更助為虐，是無天地也。

translations.literal: When bandits led by Yu Sheng rebelled in Shunchang and officials all fled, local soldier Chen Wang, who had always delighted in trouble, plotted with archer Zhang Gun to raise the fort in support; Wang rebuked them: "Our parents, wives, and children all live on state grain. Now, unable to suppress the bandits, you would aid their cruelty—this is to have no heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Sheng and other bandits rose in Shunchang and officials fled, local soldier Chen Wang, who had always courted trouble, plotted with archer Zhang Gun to hand the fort to the rebels. Wang rebuked them: "Our parents, wives, and children all live on state grain. Unable to fight the bandits, you would help them ravage the land—that is to deny heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: ”凶黨忿，剔其目而殺之。

translations.literal: " The ruffians in rage gouged out his eyes and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The ruffians gouged out his eyes and killed him in rage.

sentences.zh: 一子曰佛勝，年二十，以勇聞，賊詐以父命召之，至則俱死。

translations.literal: He had a son Fosheng, twenty years old, famed for courage; the bandits falsely summoned him in his father's name, and when he came both died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fosheng, twenty years old and famed for courage, was lured by a false message in his father's name. Father and son both died when he came.

sentences.zh: 其妻馬氏聞之，行且哭，賊脅汙之，不從，節解之。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Ma, hearing this, walked along weeping; the bandits tried to force her and she would not submit, so they dismembered her.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Ma, hearing this, walked along weeping. The bandits tried to violate her; she refused, and they dismembered her.

sentences.zh: 賊既平，旺死跡在地，隱隱不沒，邑人驚異，為設像城隍廟，歲時祭享。

translations.literal: After the bandits were suppressed, the trace of Wang's blood on the ground faintly would not disappear; the townspeople were astonished and set up his image in the City God temple, offering sacrifices each year.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits were crushed, Wang's bloodstain on the ground faintly would not fade. The townspeople were awed and set up his image in the City God temple, sacrificing to him every year.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，轉運使以狀聞，詔贈承信郎，更立祠，號忠節。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing the transport commissioner reported it; an edict posthumously made him Gentleman for Trusting in Good Faith, rebuilt the shrine, and named it Loyal Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shaoxing the transport commissioner reported the matter. The court posthumously made him Gentleman for Trusting in Good Faith, rebuilt the shrine, and named it Loyal Integrity.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，復詔立湣節廟以祠之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year another edict established the Mournful Integrity temple to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the court again ordered a Mournful Integrity temple built for his worship.

sentences.zh: 馬俊或曰進，太平州慈湖砦兵也。

translations.literal: Ma Jun—also written Jin—was a soldier of Cihu Fort in Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun—also written Jin—was a soldier at Cihu Fort in Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，砦軍陸德、周青、張順等據州叛，青為謀主，約翌日盡黥城中少壯，而屠其老弱，然後擁眾渡江。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing fort soldiers Lu De, Zhou Qing, Zhang Shun, and others seized the prefecture in rebellion; Qing was the chief plotter and planned that the next day all able-bodied youths in the city would be tattooed, the old and weak slaughtered, and then the host would cross the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing fort soldiers Lu De, Zhou Qing, Zhang Shun, and others rebelled and seized the prefecture. Qing was the chief plotter. They planned to tattoo every able-bodied youth the next day, slaughter the old and weak, then cross the Yangzi with their host.

sentences.zh: 俊隸青左右，得其謀，陰結其徒十人殺賊，然後諭眾開門，其徒許之。

translations.literal: Jun served at Qing's side, learned the plot, secretly rallied ten comrades to kill the rebels, and then urged the crowd to open the gates; his comrades agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun served at Qing's side, learned the plot, and secretly rallied ten comrades to kill the rebels, then urged the people to open the gates. His comrades agreed.

sentences.zh: 俊歸語其妻孫氏，與之訣，至南門，伺青出上馬，斫中頰，九人懼不敢前。

translations.literal: Jun went home and told his wife Lady Sun, bade her farewell, and at the south gate waited for Qing to mount; he struck Qing in the cheek, but the nine others in fear did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jun went home, told his wife Lady Sun, and bade her farewell. At the south gate he waited for Qing to mount and struck him in the cheek—but the nine others were afraid and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 俊與妻子皆遇害。

translations.literal: Jun and his wife and children were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, his wife, and his children were all killed.

sentences.zh: 青被傷臥旬日，賊黨散，官軍至，德、青遂伏誅。

translations.literal: Qing, wounded, lay abed ten days; the rebel band dispersed, government troops arrived, and De and Qing were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qing lay wounded for ten days. The rebel band broke up, government troops arrived, and De and Qing were executed.

sentences.zh: 三年，贈俊修武郎，為立祠，號登勇。

translations.literal: In the third year Jun was posthumously made Gentleman for Cultivating Martial Virtue, a shrine was built for him, and named Ascending Courage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Jun was posthumously made Gentleman for Cultivating Martial Virtue. A shrine was built for him and named Ascending Courage.

sentences.zh: 楊震仲字革父，成都府人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhenzhong, styled Gefu, was a native of Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhenzhong, styled Gefu, was from Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蚤負氣節，雅有誌當世。

translations.literal: From youth he possessed integrity and had long aspired to serve the age.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had integrity and long aspired to serve his times.

sentences.zh: 登淳熙二年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chunxi.

sentences.zh: 知閬州新井縣，以惠政聞。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Xinjin County in Langzhou he was known for benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Xinjin County in Langzhou he was known for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 辟興元府通判，權大安軍。

translations.literal: He was invited as vice prefect of Xingyuan Prefecture and acted as military commander of Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was invited to serve as vice prefect of Xingyuan Prefecture and acted as military commander of Da'an.

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，素聞震仲名，馳檄招之，震仲辭疾不行。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled, having long heard of Zhenzhong's reputation, he sent a rapid dispatch to summon him; Zhenzhong pleaded illness and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, he had long heard of Zhenzhong's reputation and sent an urgent summons. Zhenzhong pleaded illness and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 時軍教授史次秦亦被檄，謀於震仲，震仲曰：“大安自武興而來，為西蜀第一州，若首從其招，則諸郡風靡矣。

translations.literal: At that time army instructor Shi Ciqin was also summoned; he consulted Zhenzhong, who said: "Da'an, coming down from Wuxing, is the foremost prefecture in western Shu; if it is the first to accept his summons, all other prefectures will follow like the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Army instructor Shi Ciqin was summoned as well and consulted Zhenzhong. Zhenzhong said: "Da'an, reaching down from Wuxing, is the foremost prefecture in western Shu. If we are the first to answer his summons, every other prefecture will follow.

sentences.zh: 顧力不能拒，義死之。

translations.literal: Seeing that we lack the strength to resist, righteousness demands death.
translations.idiomatic: We lack the strength to resist. Righteousness demands that we die.

sentences.zh: 教授非城郭臣，且有母在，未可死，脫去為宜。

translations.literal: An instructor is not a walled-city official, and you have a mother living—you need not die; it is better to slip away.
translations.idiomatic: You are an instructor, not a walled-city official, and your mother still lives—you need not die. Better to slip away.

sentences.zh: ”因屬次秦曰：“吾死，以匹絹纏身，斂以小棺足矣。

translations.literal: " He then entrusted Ciqin: "When I die, wrap my body in a bolt of silk and a small coffin is enough.
translations.idiomatic: " He then told Ciqin: "When I die, wrap me in a bolt of silk and bury me in a small coffin—that is enough.

sentences.zh: ”曦遣興州都統司機宜郭鵬飛代震仲，趣其行益急。

translations.literal: " Xi sent Guo Pengfei of the Xingzhou command staff to replace Zhenzhong and pressed him ever more urgently to come.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi sent Guo Pengfei of the Xingzhou command staff to replace Zhenzhong and pressed him ever harder to come.

sentences.zh: 鵬飛宴震仲，終飲不見顏色。

translations.literal: Pengfei feasted Zhenzhong, but through the entire drinking he showed no change of countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Pengfei gave a feast for Zhenzhong, but through the whole banquet his face never changed.

sentences.zh: 歸舍，然燭獨坐，夜漏至三鼓，呼左右索湯，比至，震仲飲毒死矣。

translations.literal: Returning home, he lit a candle and sat alone; when the night watch reached the third drum he called for soup, and by the time it came Zhenzhong had drunk poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Back at his quarters he lit a candle and sat alone. When the third watch came he called for soup; by the time it arrived he had drunk poison and was dead.

sentences.zh: 次秦如其言，斂而置於蕭寺，闔郡為之流涕。

translations.literal: Ciqin did as he had said, buried him, and placed the body in a deserted temple; the whole prefecture wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ciqin did as he asked, buried him, and laid the body in a deserted temple. The whole prefecture wept.

sentences.zh: 震仲之未死，先遺家人書曰：“武興之事，從之則失節，何面目在世間？

translations.literal: Before Zhenzhong died he had sent his family a letter: "In the matter of Wuxing, to follow Xi is to lose integrity—what face could I show in the world?
translations.idiomatic: Before he died Zhenzhong had written his family: "In the matter of Wuxing, to follow Xi is to lose my integrity—what face could I show in the world?

sentences.zh: 不從禍立見。

translations.literal: Not to follow brings immediate disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Not to follow brings immediate ruin.

sentences.zh: 我死，禍止一身，不及妻子矣。

translations.literal: If I die, disaster stops with one man and does not reach wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: If I die, the disaster stops with me and does not reach my wife and children.

sentences.zh: 人孰無死，死而有子能自立，即不死。

translations.literal: Who does not die? To die while one's son can stand on his own is not to die.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone must die. To die while one's son can stand on his own is not truly to die.

sentences.zh: ”自震仲死，蜀之義士感慨奮發，始有協謀誅逆者。

translations.literal: " From the time of Zhenzhong's death, righteous men of Shu, stirred and inspired, first began to plot together to kill the traitor.
translations.idiomatic: " After Zhenzhong's death, righteous men of Shu, stirred to indignation, first began to plot together against the traitor.

sentences.zh: 明年，曦伏誅，蜀帥安丙、楊輔以聞，贈朝奉大夫、直寶謨閣，官二子，表其裏曰義榮。

translations.literal: The next year Xi was executed; Shu commanders An Bing and Yang Fu reported it; he was posthumously made Grand Master for Court Audience and direct academician of the Baomo Hall, two sons received office, and his home lane was titled Lane of Righteous Glory.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xi was executed. Shu commanders An Bing and Yang Fu reported Zhenzhong's death. He was posthumously made Grand Master for Court Audience and direct academician of the Baomo Hall; two sons received office, and his home lane was named Lane of Righteous Glory.

sentences.zh: 吳獵宣諭西蜀，為之請廟與諡，名其廟旌忠，諡曰節毅。

translations.literal: Wu Lie, proclaiming instructions in western Shu, requested a temple and posthumous title for him; the temple was named Commending Loyalty and the posthumous title Steadfast Resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lie, proclaiming instructions in western Shu, asked for a temple and posthumous title. The temple was named Commending Loyalty and his posthumous title was Steadfast Resolve.

sentences.zh: 史次秦，眉山人。

translations.literal: Shi Ciqin was a native of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ciqin was from Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 及進士第。

translations.literal: He attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，招次秦甚遽，次秦遷延固避，偽知大安軍郭鵬飛迫之行，乃以石灰桐油塗兩目，末生附子傅之，比至目益腫。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled he urgently summoned Ciqin; Ciqin delayed and firmly avoided going. The puppet Da'an commander Guo Pengfei forced him to travel, so he smeared lime and tung oil on both eyes and applied raw aconite; by the time he arrived his eyes had swollen worse.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled he urgently summoned Ciqin, who delayed and firmly refused. The puppet Da'an commander Guo Pengfei forced him to go. Ciqin smeared lime and tung oil on both eyes and applied raw aconite; by the time he arrived his eyes had swollen worse still.

sentences.zh: 次秦母年高而賢，聞次秦為曦所招，即命家人以疾篤馳報，且曰：“恐病不足取信，以訃聞可也。

translations.literal: Ciqin's mother, advanced in years and virtuous, hearing that Ciqin had been summoned by Xi, at once ordered the household to report by urgent dispatch that he was gravely ill, saying: "If illness alone is not credible enough, report his death.
translations.idiomatic: Ciqin's mother, elderly and virtuous, hearing that Xi had summoned her son, at once ordered the household to send urgent word that he was gravely ill, saying: "If illness alone won't convince them, report his death.

sentences.zh: ”曦乃聽還。

translations.literal: " Xi then allowed him to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi then let him return.

sentences.zh: 曦誅，蜀帥上其事，改秩為利路主管文字，仕至合州太守。

translations.literal: After Xi was executed the Shu commander reported the matter; his rank was changed to chief clerk on the Lizhou circuit and he rose to prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi was executed the Shu commander reported his conduct. Ciqin's rank was changed to chief clerk on the Lizhou circuit, and he rose to prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 有郭靖者，高橋土豪巡檢也。

translations.literal: There was a Guo Jing, a local strongman and patrol inspector of Gaoqiao.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Guo Jing, a local strongman and patrol inspector of Gaoqiao.

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，四州之民不願臣金，棄田宅，推老稚，順嘉陵而下。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled, the people of four prefectures, unwilling to submit to the Jin, abandoned fields and houses, pushing old and young before them, and drifted down the Jialing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, people in four prefectures, unwilling to serve the Jin, abandoned their fields and homes and drifted down the Jialing, old and young together.

sentences.zh: 過大安軍，楊震仲計口給粟，境內無餒死者。

translations.literal: Passing through Da'an, Yang Zhenzhong rationed grain by head count, and within the jurisdiction none starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Da'an, Yang Zhenzhong rationed grain by head count, and within his jurisdiction none starved to death.

sentences.zh: 曦盡驅驚移之民使還，皆不肯行。

translations.literal: Xi drove all these displaced people to return, but none would go.
translations.idiomatic: Xi drove all these displaced people to return, but none would go.

sentences.zh: 靖時亦在遣中，至白崖關，告其弟端曰：“吾家世為王民，自金人犯邊，吾兄弟不能以死報國，避難入關，今為曦所逐，吾不忍棄漢衣冠，願死於此，為趙氏鬼。

translations.literal: Jing was also among those being sent back; reaching Baiya Pass he told his younger brother Duan: "Our family for generations has been subjects of the throne. Since the Jurchens invaded the frontier we brothers could not repay the state with death and fled into the passes for refuge. Now driven out by Xi, I cannot bear to abandon Han dress and caps—I wish to die here and be a ghost of the Zhao house.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was among those being sent back. At Baiya Pass he told his younger brother Duan: "Our family has served the throne for generations. When the Jurchens invaded we brothers could not die for the state and fled into the passes. Now Xi drives us out. I cannot abandon Han dress and caps. I wish to die here and be a ghost of the Zhao house.

sentences.zh: ”遂赴江而死。

translations.literal: " He then threw himself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He threw himself into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 高稼，字南叔，邛州蒲江人。

translations.literal: Gao Jia, styled Nanshu, was a native of Pujiang in Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jia, styled Nanshu, was from Pujiang in Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 真德秀一見以國士期之。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu, on first meeting him, treated him as a man of national stature.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu, on first meeting him, treated him as a man of national stature.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the seventh year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Jiading.

sentences.zh: 調成都尉，轉九隴丞。

translations.literal: He was assigned as defender of Chengdu and then transferred to assistant magistrate of Jiulong.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as defender of Chengdu, then transferred to assistant magistrate of Jiulong.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，免喪，辟潼川府路都鈴轄司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: Mourning his mother, after the mourning period he was invited as handler in the Tongchuan circuit command staff.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was invited to serve as handler in the Tongchuan circuit command staff.

sentences.zh: 製置使崔與之聞其名，改辟本司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Cui Yuzhi, hearing his name, changed the appointment to handler in his own headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Cui Yuzhi, hearing his reputation, reassigned him as handler in his own headquarters.

sentences.zh: 稼持論不阿，憂世甚切，及鄭損為製置使，即求去。

translations.literal: Jia held to his views without bending and grieved deeply for the age; when Zheng Sun became pacification commissioner he at once asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jia held to his views without compromise and grieved deeply for the times. When Zheng Sun became pacification commissioner he asked to leave at once.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以稼讚閫有勞，未幾，改知綿穀縣。

translations.literal: The court, because Jia had aided the command with merit, soon changed his post to magistrate of Miangu County.
translations.idiomatic: The court, recognizing his service to the command, soon made him magistrate of Miangu County.

sentences.zh: 製置司以總領所擅十一州會子之利，請盡廢之，此蓋紹興、隆興之間得旨為之者。

translations.literal: The pacification headquarters, because the general supply office monopolized profits from huizi notes in eleven prefectures, requested their complete abolition—something that had received imperial approval between the Shaoxing and Longxing eras.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification headquarters asked to abolish huizi notes entirely because the general supply office monopolized their profits in eleven prefectures—something approved between the Shaoxing and Longxing eras.

sentences.zh: 令下，民疑，為之罷市。

translations.literal: When the order went out the people were uneasy and closed the markets in protest.
translations.idiomatic: When the order went out the people were uneasy and shut the markets in protest.

sentences.zh: 稼亟出私錢以給中下戶。

translations.literal: Jia quickly paid out private funds to supply middle and lower households.
translations.idiomatic: Jia quickly paid out his own funds to support middle and lower households.

sentences.zh: 稼弟定子時為總領所主管文字，相與征其誤而力救之，得存其半，公私僅濟。

translations.literal: Jia's younger brother Dingzi was then chief clerk in the general supply office; together they examined the error and strove to remedy it, preserving half the notes so that public and private needs were barely met.
translations.idiomatic: Jia's younger brother Dingzi was then chief clerk in the general supply office. Together they exposed the mistake and fought to remedy it, preserving half the notes so public and private needs were barely met.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，有司置弗聞，稼捐橐中裝，市粟以食之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine the authorities paid no heed; Jia donated his traveling funds, bought grain, and fed the people, saving very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of great famine the authorities ignored the crisis. Jia donated his traveling funds, bought grain, and fed the people, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 損之入蜀也，稼同產弟了翁誦言於朝，謂必敗事。

translations.literal: When Sun entered Shu, Jia's full brother Liaoweng spoke repeatedly at court that he was sure to ruin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun entered Shu, Jia's full brother Liaoweng repeatedly told the court that Sun was sure to ruin affairs.

sentences.zh: 損銜之，遂劾稼罷。

translations.literal: Sun bore a grudge and therefore impeached Jia, who was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun resented this and impeached Jia, who was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 寶慶三年，元兵至武階，損棄沔而遁。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing, Yuan troops reached Wujie; Sun abandoned Mian and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing Yuan troops reached Wujie. Sun abandoned Mian and fled.

sentences.zh: 桂如淵鎮蜀，辟通判沔州，尋檄兼幕職。

translations.literal: Gui Ruyuan commanded Shu and invited Jia as vice prefect of Mianzhou; soon he was ordered to serve concurrently on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui Ruyuan took command in Shu he invited Jia as vice prefect of Mianzhou and soon added him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 稼首言：“蜀以三關為門戶，五州為藩籬，自前帥棄五州，民無固誌，一旦敵至，又有因糧之利，或遂留不去。

translations.literal: Jia spoke first: "Shu takes the three passes as its gates and the five prefectures as its screen. Since the former commander abandoned the five prefectures the people have had no firm resolve; once the enemy arrives, with the advantage of foraging grain, they may stay and not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jia spoke first: "Shu relies on the three passes as its gates and the five prefectures as its screen. Since the former commander abandoned those five prefectures the people have lost their resolve. Once the enemy comes, with grain to forage, they may simply stay.

sentences.zh: 今亟當申理，俾緩急有所保聚。

translations.literal: Now we must urgently set things in order so that in crisis there are places to gather and defend.
translations.idiomatic: We must set this right at once so that in crisis there are places to gather and hold.

sentences.zh: ”如淵然之，乃創山砦八十有四，且募義兵五千人，與民約曰：“敵至則官軍守原堡，民丁保山砦，義兵為遊擊，庶其前靡所掠，後弗容久。

translations.literal: " Ruyuan agreed and therefore established eighty-four mountain forts and recruited five thousand volunteer troops, agreeing with the people: "When the enemy comes the regular army will hold the plain forts, the militia will hold the mountain forts, and the volunteers will strike as raiders—so that in front they have nothing to plunder and in the rear they cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruyuan agreed. He built eighty-four mountain forts and recruited five thousand volunteers, telling the people: "When the enemy comes the regular army holds the plain forts, the militia holds the mountain forts, and the volunteers strike as raiders—so they cannot plunder ahead or linger behind.

sentences.zh: 北兵由東道以入，如淵憂之，辟稼知洋州。

translations.literal: Northern troops entered by the eastern route; Ruyuan was worried and appointed Jia prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops entered by the eastern route. Ruyuan, worried, appointed Jia prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 稼日夜為守禦計，以洋居平地，無一卒以守，議移金州帥司軍千人駐洋州，而自任其餉給。

translations.literal: Jia day and night made plans for defense; because Yang lay on flat ground with not a single soldier to guard it, he proposed moving a thousand men from the Jinzhou command to garrison Yang and undertook their provisions himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jia worked day and night on defense. Yang lay on flat ground with no garrison, so he proposed moving a thousand men from the Jinzhou command to Yang and paid their provisions himself.

sentences.zh: 李心傳為言諸朝，不報。

translations.literal: Li Xinzhuan spoke of it at court; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xinzhuan pleaded the case at court, but nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 及鳳州破，製置司始從稼請，調金州兵赴之，而兵不時至。

translations.literal: When Fengzhou fell the pacification headquarters at last followed Jia's request and transferred Jinzhou troops, but they did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengzhou fell the pacification headquarters at last approved Jia's request and ordered Jinzhou troops forward, but they did not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 漢中陷，梁、洋之民數十萬盡趨安康。

translations.literal: Hanzhong fell; several hundred thousand people of Liang and Yang all fled toward Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong fell. Several hundred thousand people from Liang and Yang fled toward Ankang.

sentences.zh: 稼乃移屯黃金渡，收散卒，招忠義，以製置司之命，致故將陳昱於安康，委以收復之任。

translations.literal: Jia then moved his camp to Huangjin Ford, gathered scattered troops, recruited loyal volunteers, and by pacification headquarters order brought the former general Chen Yu to Ankang, entrusting him with the task of recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Jia moved to Huangjin Ford, gathered scattered troops, recruited loyal volunteers, and by order of the pacification headquarters brought former general Chen Yu to Ankang to lead recovery.

sentences.zh: 昱部分諸軍，召青座、華陽諸關守將，皆以兵來會，凡得三千人，稼竭洋之帑廩贍之。

translations.literal: Yu deployed the armies and summoned garrison commanders of Qingzuo, Huayang, and other passes; all came with troops, totaling three thousand men, whom Jia fed at the expense of Yang's treasury to the last grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yu deployed the armies and summoned garrison commanders from Qingzuo, Huayang, and other passes. Three thousand men answered. Jia emptied Yang's treasury to feed them.

sentences.zh: 以州事付通判，而自假節製軍馬，督諸將繼進。

translations.literal: He handed prefectural affairs to the vice prefect and himself took credentials to command the armies, urging the generals to advance.
translations.idiomatic: He handed prefectural affairs to the vice prefect, took credentials to command the armies himself, and urged the generals forward.

sentences.zh: 沔州破，北兵迫大安，益昌大震，稼亟命趨沔，自至西縣援之。

translations.literal: When Mianzhou fell northern troops pressed on Da'an and Yichang was greatly shaken; Jia urgently ordered a rush to Mian and himself went to Xixian to reinforce it.
translations.idiomatic: When Mianzhou fell northern troops pressed Da'an and Yichang panicked. Jia ordered a rush to Mian and went himself to Xixian to reinforce it.

sentences.zh: 如淵以便宜命稼利路提刑司兼權興元府，製置司檄其守米倉，稼移書曰：“今日之事如弈棋，所校者先後爾。

translations.literal: Ruyuan by emergency authority made Jia Lizhou judicial intendant and acting prefect of Xingyuan; the pacification headquarters ordered him to hold Micang. Jia wrote: "Today's affair is like a game of chess—what matters is who moves first.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyuan by emergency authority made Jia Lizhou judicial intendant and acting prefect of Xingyuan. The pacification headquarters ordered him to hold Micang. Jia wrote: "Today's affair is like chess—what matters is who moves first.

sentences.zh: 苟以分水、三泉、米倉為可保，敵兵若自宕昌、清川以入，將孰禦之？

translations.literal: If we think Fenghsui, Sanquan, and Micang can be held secure, and enemy troops enter from Dangchang and Qingchuan, who will stop them?
translations.idiomatic: If we think Fenghsui, Sanquan, and Micang are safe, and the enemy enters from Dangchang and Qingchuan, who will stop them?

sentences.zh: 盍以興、沔、利三戎司分駐鳳州，俾製司已招之忠義、關表復仇之豪傑，聯司以進，兵氣奪矣。

translations.literal: Why not station the three Xing, Mian, and Li garrison commands at Fengzhou separately, join the loyal volunteers already recruited by the pacification headquarters and the frontier heroes seeking revenge, and advance together—the enemy's morale would be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Why not station the Xing, Mian, and Li garrison commands at Fengzhou, join the loyal volunteers and frontier heroes already recruited, and advance together? The enemy's spirit would break.

sentences.zh: ”如淵遲疑不決。

translations.literal: " Ruyuan hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruyuan hesitated and would not decide.

sentences.zh: 逮天水、同慶被屠，西和圍益急，始會軍民之眾萬人援之，道梗不得前，而城已破矣。

translations.literal: When Tianshui and Tongqing were massacred and the siege of Xihe grew urgent, he at last assembled ten thousand troops and civilians to relieve it, but the road was blocked and they could not advance—and the city had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianshui and Tongqing were massacred and Xihe's siege tightened, he at last assembled ten thousand troops and civilians to relieve it—but the road was blocked, they could not advance, and the city had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 俄報砦窠、七方之師皆潰，稼率遺民駐廉水縣，召集保甲，分布間道，以保巴山。

translations.literal: Soon word came that the Zhaikuo and Qifang armies had all broken; Jia led the surviving people to garrison Lianshui County, summoned militia, and posted them on hidden routes to protect Mount Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the Zhaikuo and Qifang armies had collapsed. Jia led survivors to Lianshui County, summoned militia, and posted them on hidden routes to hold Mount Ba.

sentences.zh: 當是時，文臣之在軍中者惟稼一人。

translations.literal: At that time Jia was the only civil official in the army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jia was the only civil official still with the army.

sentences.zh: 如淵既罷，李代之，以稼久勞，請改畀內郡，差知榮州。

translations.literal: After Ruyuan was dismissed, Li Zhu replaced him; because Jia had long labored, he requested transfer to an interior prefecture and Jia was assigned to Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruyuan was dismissed, Li Zhu replaced him. Seeing Jia's long service, he asked to move him inland and assigned him to Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史汪剛中，如淵黨也，欲使稼分其罪，乃謂蜀之敗實由稼，遽罷之，又削二官。

translations.literal: Palace Censor Wang Gangzhong, a partisan of Ruyuan, wanted Jia to share the blame and therefore said Shu had actually been defeated because of Jia; he was abruptly dismissed and two ranks were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Wang Gangzhong, Ruyuan's partisan, wanted Jia to share the blame and claimed Shu had fallen because of Jia. Jia was abruptly dismissed and stripped of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 李心傳見上，訟稼無罪，不當罷。

translations.literal: Li Xinzhuan saw the emperor and argued that Jia was innocent and should not have been dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xinzhuan saw the emperor and argued that Jia was innocent and should not have been dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使黃伯固辟稼知閬州。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Huang Bogu invited Jia as prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Huang Bogu invited Jia to serve as prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，伯固去官，製置使趙彥呐以參議官辟之。

translations.literal: Before long Bogu left office and Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yan'na invited him as deliberation officer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bogu left office and Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yan'na invited him as deliberation officer.

sentences.zh: 製置司近漢中，稼言漢中蕩無藩籬，宜經理仙人原以為緩急視師之地。

translations.literal: The pacification headquarters was near Hanzhong; Jia said Hanzhong was stripped of its screen and that Xianren Plain should be organized as a place to observe the army in emergency.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification headquarters lay near Hanzhong. Jia said Hanzhong had lost its defenses and that Xianren Plain should be prepared as an emergency command post.

sentences.zh: 彥呐以委稼，稼至原，繕營壘，峙芻糧，比器甲，開泉源，守禦之規，罔不備具。

translations.literal: Yan'na entrusted it to Jia; arriving at the plain, Jia repaired ramparts, stockpiled fodder and grain, compared weapons and armor, opened springs—every rule of defense was fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'na entrusted the work to Jia. At the plain Jia repaired ramparts, stockpiled fodder and grain, inspected arms, opened springs—every measure of defense was ready.

sentences.zh: 會召還，彥呐密奏留稼，以直秘閣知沔州、利州提點刑獄兼參議官。

translations.literal: When he was summoned back, Yan'na secretly memorialized to keep Jia, making him direct academician of the Secretariat, prefect of Mianzhou, Lizhou judicial intendant, and deliberation officer.
translations.idiomatic: When recall was ordered, Yan'na secretly asked to keep Jia, appointing him direct academician of the Secretariat, prefect of Mianzhou, Lizhou judicial intendant, and deliberation officer.

sentences.zh: 始至，告於神曰：“郡當兵難之後，生聚撫摩，所當盡力，去之日，誓垂橐以入劍門。

translations.literal: On first arrival he told the spirits: "This prefecture faces the aftermath of war; gathering the people and soothing them is what I must exhaust myself for. On the day I leave I swear to enter Jianmen with empty purse.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he told the spirits: "This prefecture faces the aftermath of war. I must do all I can to gather and comfort the people. When I leave I swear to enter Jianmen with an empty purse.

sentences.zh: ”乃葺理創殘，招集流散，民皆繈負來歸。

translations.literal: " He then repaired the ruins, gathered the displaced, and the people all came back carrying their children.
translations.idiomatic: " He repaired the ruins, gathered the displaced, and the people returned carrying their children on their backs.

sentences.zh: 北兵入西和，薄階州，稼讚彥呐登原督戰。

translations.literal: Northern troops entered Xihe and pressed Jiezhou; Jia urged Yan'na to ascend the plain and direct the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops entered Xihe and pressed Jiezhou. Jia urged Yan'na to take the plain and direct the battle.

sentences.zh: 知天水軍曹友聞等兵大戰。

translations.literal: Cao Youwen, commander of Tianshui Army, and others fought a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Youwen of Tianshui Army and others fought a great battle.

sentences.zh: 進稼三官，為朝請大夫兼關外四州安撫司公事，措置西路屯田。

translations.literal: Jia was advanced three ranks, made Gentleman for Court Audience with concurrent duty in the four outer-prefecture pacification office and charged with organizing western-route military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was advanced three ranks, made Gentleman for Court Audience with duty in the four outer-prefecture pacification office and charged with organizing western-route military colonies.

sentences.zh: 稼嚐代彥呐論蜀事利害，上嘉覽之。

translations.literal: Jia once wrote in Yan'na's place on the advantages and dangers of Shu affairs; the emperor read it with approval.
translations.idiomatic: Jia once drafted a memorial for Yan'na on the dangers facing Shu; the emperor read it with approval.

sentences.zh: 北兵自鳳州入，東軍不能禦，遂搗河池，至西池穀，距沔九十里。

translations.literal: Northern troops entered from Fengzhou; the eastern army could not stop them and struck at Hechi, reaching Xichigu, ninety li from Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops entered from Fengzhou. The eastern army could not stop them and struck Hechi, reaching Xichigu ninety li from Mian.

sentences.zh: 吏民率逃，議欲退保大安。

translations.literal: Officials and people fled in droves; there was talk of retreating to hold Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people fled. Some urged retreat to Da'an.

sentences.zh: 稼白彥呐曰：“今日之事，有進無退，能進據險地，以身捍蜀，敵有後顧，必不深入；

translations.literal: Jia told Yan'na: "In today's affair there is advance but no retreat. If we can advance and hold rugged ground, using our bodies to shield Shu, the enemy will look to their rear and surely not press deep;
translations.idiomatic: Jia told Yan'na: "Today we advance or we die. If we seize rugged ground and shield Shu with our bodies, the enemy will watch their rear and not press deep;

sentences.zh: 若倉皇召兵，退守內地，敵長驅而前，蜀事去矣。

translations.literal: if we hastily summon troops and retreat to the interior, the enemy will drive straight forward and Shu is lost.
translations.idiomatic: if we panic, summon troops, and fall back inland, the enemy will drive straight through and Shu is lost.

sentences.zh: ”彥呐曰：“吾誌也。

translations.literal: " Yan'na said: "That is my resolve too.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan'na said: "That is my resolve as well.

sentences.zh: ”已而竟行，留稼守沔。

translations.literal: " But in the end he went anyway and left Jia to hold Mian.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet in the end he went anyway and left Jia to hold Mian.

sentences.zh: 北兵自白水關入六股株，距沔六十里。

translations.literal: Northern troops entered Liuguzhu from Baishui Pass, sixty li from Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops entered Liuguzhu from Baishui Pass, sixty li from Mian.

sentences.zh: 沔無城，依山為阻，稼升高鼓噪，盛旗鼓為疑兵。

translations.literal: Mian had no walls and relied on the mountains for defense; Jia climbed high, beat drums and shouted, and displayed banners and drums as a deception.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had no walls and relied on the mountains. Jia climbed high, beat drums, shouted, and displayed banners as a deception.

sentences.zh: 彥呐至置口，輟帳前總管和彥威，以軍還沔，召小將楊俊、何璘悉以兵會，又調總管王宣精兵千人益之。

translations.literal: Yan'na reached Zhikou, relieved Front Army Commander He Yanwei, returned with troops to Mian, summoned junior generals Yang Jun and He Lin with all their forces, and transferred a thousand elite troops under Commander Wang Xuan to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'na reached Zhikou, relieved Front Army Commander He Yanwei, returned to Mian with troops, summoned junior generals Yang Jun and He Lin with all their men, and added a thousand elite troops under Commander Wang Xuan.

sentences.zh: 璘軍無紀律，稼捕其縱火者三人，誅之。

translations.literal: Lin's army lacked discipline; Jia arrested three arsonists and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's army was undisciplined. Jia arrested three arsonists and executed them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，北兵大至，璘遁。

translations.literal: Before long northern troops came in force and Lin fled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long northern troops came in force and Lin fled.

sentences.zh: 其眾皆潰，遂下沔州。

translations.literal: His host all broke; Mianzhou then fell.
translations.idiomatic: His men collapsed and Mianzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 先是，友聞戍七方，知沔不可守，勸稼移保山砦，而自將所部助之。

translations.literal: Earlier Youwen had garrisoned Qifang, knew Mian could not be held, and urged Jia to move to the mountain forts while he himself led his command to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Youwen had garrisoned Qifang. Knowing Mian could not be held, he urged Jia to move to the mountain forts while he led his own command to help.

sentences.zh: 稼曰：“七方要地，不可棄，吾郡將也，城亦不可棄。

translations.literal: Jia said: "Qifang is a vital place and cannot be abandoned. I am the prefect— the city also cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jia said: "Qifang is vital and cannot be abandoned. I am the prefect—the city cannot be abandoned either.

sentences.zh: 即事不濟，有死而已。

translations.literal: If the affair fails, death is all there is.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, there is only death.

sentences.zh: ”先二日，子斯得侍，以時危任重為憂，稼舉田承君“五日不汗”之言語之，且曰：“吾得死所，何憾！

translations.literal: " Two days earlier his son Side had attended him, worried about the peril of the times and the weight of responsibility; Jia cited Tian Chengjun's words "five days without sweating" and said: "I have found where to die—what regret is there!
translations.idiomatic: " Two days earlier his son Side had visited, worried by the crisis and his father's burden. Jia cited Tian Chengjun's words about "five days without sweating" and said: "I have found where to die—what regret is there!

sentences.zh: ”又以書告李心傳曰：“稼必堅守沔，無沔則無蜀矣。

translations.literal: " He also wrote Li Xinzhuan: "Jia will surely hold Mian fast—without Mian there is no Shu.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote Li Xinzhuan: "Jia will hold Mian to the end. Without Mian there is no Shu.

sentences.zh: 自謂此舉可以無負知己。

translations.literal: He considered that by this act he could fail no friend who knew him.
translations.idiomatic: He believed that by this act he would not fail those who trusted him.

sentences.zh: ”及事迫，參議楊約勸稼姑保大安，稼厲聲曰：“我以監司守城郭，爾以幕客往來應援，各行其誌。

translations.literal: " When the crisis pressed, Deliberation Officer Yang Yue urged Jia to hold Da'an for the moment; Jia said in a stern voice: "I as intendant guard the walled city; you as staff officer go back and forth to support—each of us follows his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " When crisis came, deliberation officer Yang Yue urged Jia to fall back to Da'an. Jia said sharply: "I as intendant guard this city; you as staff officer go back and forth to support—each of us follows his own resolve.

sentences.zh: ”常平司屬官馮元章率吏士力請稼少避，稼不為動。

translations.literal: " Ever-Normal Granary subordinate Feng Yuanzhang led clerks and soldiers to beg Jia to withdraw a little; Jia was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: " Ever-Normal Granary officer Feng Yuanzhang led clerks and soldiers to beg Jia to withdraw briefly. Jia would not budge.

sentences.zh: 城既陷，眾擁稼出戶，稼叱之不能止，兵騎四集圍之，遂死焉。

translations.literal: When the city fell the crowd pushed Jia out the gate; he shouted at them but could not stop them; cavalry surrounded him on all sides and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the crowd pushed him out the gate. He shouted but could not stop them. Cavalry surrounded him on all sides and he died.

sentences.zh: 詔進稼七官，為正議大夫、龍圖閣直學士，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Jia seven ranks, made him Grand Master for Discussion of Policy and direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and gave the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The court advanced Jia seven ranks, made him Grand Master for Discussion of Policy and direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 後以子斯得執政，累贈太師。

translations.literal: Later, because his son Side attained high office, he was repeatedly posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his son Side rose to high office, he was repeatedly posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 稼為人慷慨有大誌，聞人有善，稱之不容口；

translations.literal: Jia as a man was generous and had great resolve; hearing of someone's good quality he praised it without cease;
translations.idiomatic: Jia was generous and ambitious. When he heard of someone's virtue he praised it without end;

sentences.zh: 不善，麵折無所避。

translations.literal: if it was bad, he rebuked to the face without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: when he saw fault he rebuked it to the face without flinching.

sentences.zh: 推轂人士，常恐不及，視財如糞土。

translations.literal: He promoted men of talent, always fearing he had not done enough, and regarded wealth as dirt.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted talent and always feared he had not done enough. He treated wealth like dirt.

sentences.zh: 死之日，聞者莫不於邑流涕。

translations.literal: On the day of his death all who heard wept in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died all who heard wept.

sentences.zh: 所著有《縮齋類槁》三十卷。
