translations.literal: His writings include thirty juan of Collected Drafts of the Contracted Studio.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include thirty juan of Collected Drafts of the Contracted Studio.

sentences.zh: 斯得自有傳。

translations.literal: Side has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Side has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 曹友聞，字允叔，同慶栗亭人。

translations.literal: Cao Youwen, styled Yunshu, was a native of Litings in Tongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Youwen, styled Yunshu, was from Litings in Tongqing.

sentences.zh: 武惠王彬十二世孫也。

translations.literal: He was a twelfth-generation descendant of Prince Wu Hui, Cao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He was a twelfth-generation descendant of Prince Wu Hui, Cao Bin.

sentences.zh: 少有大誌，與仲弟友諒不遠千里尋師取友。

translations.literal: From youth he had great resolve; with his second younger brother Youliang he traveled a thousand li seeking teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had great resolve. With his second brother Youliang he traveled far seeking teachers and friends.

sentences.zh: 登寶慶二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 授綿竹尉，改辟天水軍教授。

translations.literal: He was appointed defender of Mianzhu and then invited as instructor of Tianshui Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed defender of Mianzhu, then invited as instructor of Tianshui Army.

sentences.zh: 城已被圍，友聞單騎夜入，與守臣張維糾民厲戰。

translations.literal: The city was already besieged; Youwen entered alone by night on horseback and with the defender Zhang Wei rallied the people to fight fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The city was already besieged. Youwen rode in alone by night and with defender Zhang Wei rallied the people to fight fiercely.

sentences.zh: 兵退，製置使製大旗，書“滿身膽”以旌之。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew the pacification commissioner made a great banner inscribed "Courage in Every Fiber" to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew the pacification commissioner made a great banner inscribed "Courage in Every Fiber" to honor him.

sentences.zh: 已而兵復至，友聞罄家財招集忠義，得健士五千人。

translations.literal: Before long troops came again; Youwen spent his entire family fortune recruiting loyal volunteers and obtained five thousand stalwart men.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy returned. Youwen spent his entire family fortune recruiting loyal volunteers and raised five thousand stalwart men.

sentences.zh: 製置使李檄管忠義，領所部守仙人關，且行且戰，至峽口據險。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Li Zhu ordered him to command the loyal volunteers, led his command to hold Xianren Pass, fought as he marched, and at Xiakou seized rugged ground.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Li Zhu ordered him to command the loyal volunteers. He led his men to hold Xianren Pass, fought as he marched, and seized rugged ground at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 前軍統製屈信率所部突陣，還所掠四州人畜。

translations.literal: Front Army Commander Qu Xin led his command in a charge and recovered people and livestock plundered from four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Front Army Commander Qu Xin led a charge and recovered people and livestock plundered from four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 至秦填，遣左軍統製杜午迎擊，力不能敵。

translations.literal: At Qintian he sent Left Army Commander Du Wu to meet the attack, but their strength could not match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Qintian he sent Left Army Commander Du Wu to meet the attack, but they could not match the enemy.

sentences.zh: 友聞令諸軍乘高據險，身冒矢石，為士卒先。

translations.literal: Youwen ordered the armies to seize high and rugged ground, himself braving arrows and stones and going before the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen ordered his armies to seize high ground, braved arrows and stones himself, and went before his men.

sentences.zh: 信與統製張安國領兵出戰。

translations.literal: Xin and Commander Zhang Anguo led troops out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Commander Zhang Anguo led troops out to battle.

sentences.zh: 兵退，製置使檄捍七方關。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew the pacification commissioner ordered him to defend Qifang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew the pacification commissioner ordered him to defend Qifang Pass.

sentences.zh: 北兵東破武休關，已而破七方，遂入沔州金牛，至大安，又分兵自嘉陵江木皮口突出何進軍後，進戰敗死之，遂長驅入劍門。

translations.literal: Northern troops broke Wuxiu Pass in the east, then broke Qifang, entered Mianzhou at Jinniu, reached Da'an, and sent a detachment from Mupikou on the Jialing to strike behind He Jin's army; Jin was defeated and killed, and they drove straight into Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops broke Wuxiu Pass in the east, then Qifang, entered Mianzhou at Jinniu, reached Da'an, and sent a detachment from Mupikou on the Jialing to strike behind He Jin's army. Jin was defeated and killed, and they drove straight into Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 友聞與弟萬各率所部，取間道過氈帽山，至青蒿埧，戰於白水江中流。

translations.literal: Youwen and his younger brother Wan each led their commands by hidden routes over Zhanmao Mountain to Qinghao Dam and fought in midstream on the Baishui River.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen and his younger brother Wan each led their commands by hidden routes over Zhanmao Mountain to Qinghao Dam and fought in midstream on the Baishui River.

sentences.zh: 兵退，製置司檄駐閬州。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew the pacification headquarters ordered him to garrison Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew the pacification headquarters ordered him to garrison Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 叛將魯珍為陳隆之所斬，珍部曲肆焚劫，友聞討斬其將郭虎、藺廣、楊仲等，餘黨散去。

translations.literal: The rebel general Lu Zhen was beheaded by Chen Longzhi; Zhen's followers wantonly burned and plundered; Youwen pursued and beheaded his generals Guo Hu, Lin Guang, Yang Zhong, and others, and the rest dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Lu Zhen was beheaded by Chen Longzhi. Zhen's followers burned and plundered at will. Youwen pursued and beheaded generals Guo Hu, Lin Guang, Yang Zhong, and others, and the rest dispersed.

sentences.zh: 檄知天水軍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to command Tianshui Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to command Tianshui Army.

sentences.zh: 北兵入鳳州，略河池，抵同慶。

translations.literal: Northern troops entered Fengzhou, overran Hechi, and reached Tongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops entered Fengzhou, overran Hechi, and reached Tongqing.

sentences.zh: 友聞密遣統製王漢臣、統領張祥，授以方略出戰。

translations.literal: Youwen secretly sent Commanders Wang Hanchen and Zhang Xiang with battle plans to go out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen secretly sent Commanders Wang Hanchen and Zhang Xiang with battle plans to engage the enemy.

sentences.zh: 兵至城下，友聞部分諸將各守一門，偃旗伏鼓，戒士卒，俟漸近，鳴鼓張旗，矢石並發。

translations.literal: When troops reached the walls Youwen assigned each general to guard one gate, lowered banners and hid drums, warned the soldiers to wait until the enemy drew near, then beat drums, raised banners, and loosed arrows and stones together.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached the walls Youwen assigned each general one gate, lowered banners and hid drums, and told his men to wait until the enemy drew near—then beat drums, raise banners, and unleash arrows and stones together.

sentences.zh: 又命漢臣等取間道出戰，自提重兵尾敵後，大戰有功。

translations.literal: He also ordered Hanchen and others to strike by hidden routes while he himself led heavy troops to follow the enemy's rear—a great battle with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Hanchen and others to strike by hidden routes while he led heavy troops to follow the enemy's rear—a great victory.

sentences.zh: 端平初，友聞遣萬與忠義總管時當可分兵碎石頭、青蒿穀，前後大戰數合。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping, Youwen sent Wan with Loyalty Commander Shi Dangke to divide forces at Shitou and Qinghaogu; they fought several great battles back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duanping, Youwen sent Wan with Loyalty Commander Shi Dangke to divide forces at Shitou and Qinghaogu. They fought several great battles.

sentences.zh: 製置使上其功，特授承務郎，權發遣天水軍。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner reported his merit; he was specially made Gentleman for Attending to Affairs with acting authority over Tianshui Army.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner reported his merit. He was specially made Gentleman for Attending to Affairs with acting authority over Tianshui Army.

sentences.zh: 北兵又自西和至階州，友聞曰：“階雖非吾境，豈可坐視而不救。

translations.literal: Northern troops again came from Xihe to Jiezhou; Youwen said: "Jie is not my territory, but how can I sit and watch without rescuing it?
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops again came from Xihe toward Jiezhou. Youwen said: "Jie is not my territory, but how can I sit and watch without helping?

sentences.zh: ”遂引兵與諸軍會。

translations.literal: " He therefore led troops to join the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his troops to join the other armies.

sentences.zh: 命前軍統製全貴領所部為先鋒，統製夏用出其左，張成出其右，總管陳庚及萬、友諒往來督戰。

translations.literal: He ordered Front Army Commander Quan Gui to lead his command as vanguard, Commander Xia Yong to strike on the left, Zhang Cheng on the right, and Loyalty Commander Chen Geng together with Wan and Youliang to go back and forth directing the battle.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Front Army Commander Quan Gui as vanguard, Commander Xia Yong on the left, Zhang Cheng on the right, and Loyalty Commander Chen Geng with Wan and Youliang to direct the battle back and forth.

sentences.zh: 有功，製置使趙彥呐俾節製利帥司軍馬，任責措置邊麵，換武翼大夫、閣門宣讚舍人，差權利州駐紮御前諸軍都統製，駐紮石門，控扼七方關。

translations.literal: With merit achieved, Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yan'na gave him authority over Lizhou command troops, responsibility for frontier provisions, changed his rank to Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and Palace Proclamation Attendant, and assigned him acting commander of imperial armies garrisoned in Lizhou, stationed at Shimen to control Qifang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After this success Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yan'na gave him authority over Lizhou command troops and responsibility for frontier provisions, made him Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and Palace Proclamation Attendant, and assigned him acting commander of imperial armies at Shimen to hold Qifang Pass.

sentences.zh: 明年，北兵破武休關，入沔陽，利路提刑高稼死之。

translations.literal: The next year northern troops broke Wuxiu Pass, entered Mianyang, and Lizhou judicial intendant Gao Jia died there.
translations.idiomatic: The next year northern troops broke Wuxiu Pass, entered Mianyang, and Lizhou judicial intendant Gao Jia died defending Mian.

sentences.zh: 製置使進屯青野原，被圍，友聞曰：“青野為蜀咽喉，不可緩。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner advanced to garrison Qingye Plain and was besieged; Youwen said: "Qingye is the throat of Shu—it cannot be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner advanced to Qingye Plain and was besieged. Youwen said: "Qingye is the throat of Shu—we cannot delay.

sentences.zh: ”遣萬領兵自冷水口度嘉陵江至六股株，屢戰有功。

translations.literal: " He sent Wan to lead troops from Lengshuikou across the Jialing to Liuguzhu, fighting repeatedly with merit.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Wan from Lengshuikou across the Jialing to Liuguzhu, where he fought repeatedly with success.

sentences.zh: 夜銜枚由間道直趨青野原，製置使奇萬之勇，令督諸軍戰守。

translations.literal: By night, gags in their mouths, they took a hidden route straight to Qingye Plain; the pacification commissioner marveled at Wan's courage and ordered him to direct all armies in attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: By night, with gags in their mouths, they took a hidden route straight to Qingye Plain. The pacification commissioner marveled at Wan's courage and ordered him to direct all armies in attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 兵退，友聞引精兵亦趨至原下，夜半截戰，圍遂得解。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew Youwen also led elite troops to the foot of the plain; at midnight they struck in interception and the siege was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew Youwen led elite troops to the foot of the plain. At midnight they struck and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 特授武德大夫、左驍騎大將軍，依舊利州駐紮御前諸軍統製。

translations.literal: He was specially made Grand Master of Martial Virtue and Left General of the Valiant Cavalry, continuing as commander of imperial armies garrisoned in Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially made Grand Master of Martial Virtue and Left General of the Valiant Cavalry, continuing as commander of imperial armies garrisoned in Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 北兵破沔州，搗大安，友聞遣摧鋒軍統製王資、踏白軍統製白再興速趨雞冠隘，左軍統製王進據陽平關。

translations.literal: Northern troops broke Mianzhou and struck at Da'an; Youwen sent Vanguard Army Commander Wang Zi and White Banner Army Commander Bai Zaixing to hurry to Jiguan Pass and Left Army Commander Wang Jin to hold Yangping Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops broke Mianzhou and struck Da'an. Youwen sent Vanguard commander Wang Zi and White Banner commander Bai Zaixing to Jiguan Pass and Left Army commander Wang Jin to Yangping Pass.

sentences.zh: 友聞登溪嶺，手執五方旗，指麾甫畢，兵數萬突至陽平關，遂遣進及遊奕部將王剛出戰，又親帥帳兵及背嵬軍突出陣前，左右馳射。

translations.literal: Youwen ascended Xiling, held the five-direction banner in hand, and had barely finished directing when tens of thousands of troops suddenly reached Yangping Pass; he sent Jin and Patrol general Wang Gang out to fight, then personally led his guard and Back-Awry troops to burst before the line and gallop shooting left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen climbed Xiling with the five-direction banner in hand. He had barely finished directing when tens of thousands of enemy troops reached Yangping Pass. He sent Jin and patrol general Wang Gang out to fight, then led his guard and Back-Awry troops forward to gallop and shoot on both flanks.

sentences.zh: 兵退，友聞謂忠義總管陳庚及當可曰：“敵必旋兵攻雞冠隘，宜急援之。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew Youwen told Loyalty Commander Chen Geng and Dangke: "The enemy will surely turn to attack Jiguan Pass—we must relieve it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew Youwen told Loyalty Commander Chen Geng and Dangke: "The enemy will surely turn on Jiguan Pass. We must relieve it at once.

sentences.zh: ”既而果以步騎萬餘攻隘，庚以騎兵五百直前決戰，當可將步兵左右翼並進，王資、白再興又自隘出戰，蹀血十餘里，兵乃解去。

translations.literal: " Sure enough more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry attacked the pass; Geng with five hundred cavalry charged straight ahead for decisive battle, Dangke led infantry on both wings together, and Wang Zi and Bai Zaixing also sallied from the pass—blood trampled for more than ten li before the troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " More than ten thousand infantry and cavalry attacked the pass. Geng charged with five hundred cavalry. Dangke advanced infantry on both wings. Wang Zi and Bai Zaixing sallied from the pass. Blood soaked the ground for more than ten li before the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 特授友聞眉州防禦使，依舊左驍衛大將軍、利州駐紮御前諸軍統製，兼沔州駐紮，兼管關外四州安撫，權知沔州，節製本府屯戍軍馬。

translations.literal: Youwen was specially made Defender of Meizhou, continuing as Left General of the Valiant Guard and commander of imperial armies in Lizhou, concurrently garrisoned in Mianzhou, concurrently in charge of pacification of the four outer prefectures, acting prefect of Mianzhou, and controller of garrison troops of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen was specially made Defender of Meizhou, continuing as Left General of the Valiant Guard and commander of imperial armies in Lizhou, with concurrent garrison at Mianzhou, charge of the four outer-prefecture pacification office, acting prefect of Mianzhou, and command of its garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 弟萬差知同慶府、四川製置司帳前總管，仍舊總管忠義軍馬，節製屯戍軍馬，董仙駐紮，專與沔、利兩司同共任責措置邊麵。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wan was assigned to know Tongqing Prefecture and serve as Front Headquarters Commander of the Sichuan Pacification Commission, continuing to command loyal volunteer troops, control garrison troops, garrison Dongxian, and share with the Mian and Li commands responsibility for frontier provisions.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wan was assigned to Tongqing Prefecture and as front headquarters commander of the Sichuan Pacification Commission, continuing to command loyal volunteers and garrison troops at Dongxian, sharing with the Mian and Li commands responsibility for frontier provisions.

sentences.zh: 明年，友聞引兵扼仙人關。

translations.literal: The next year Youwen led troops to hold Xianren Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Youwen led troops to hold Xianren Pass.

sentences.zh: 諜聞北兵合西夏、女真、回回、吐蕃、渤海軍五十餘萬大至，友聞語萬曰：“國家安危，在此一舉，眾寡不敵，豈容浪戰。

translations.literal: Spies reported northern troops combining Western Xia, Jurchen, Hui, Tibetan, and Bohai forces—more than five hundred thousand coming in force; Youwen told Wan: "The state's safety hangs on this one move; we cannot match their numbers—how can we fight recklessly?
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported northern armies combining Western Xia, Jurchen, Hui, Tibetan, and Bohai forces—more than five hundred thousand strong. Youwen told Wan: "The state's safety hangs on this battle. We cannot match their numbers—how can we fight recklessly?

sentences.zh: 惟當乘高據險，出奇匿伏以待之。

translations.literal: We must seize high ground, hold rugged terrain, and use hidden ambushes to await them.
translations.idiomatic: We must seize high ground, hold rugged terrain, and wait in hidden ambush.

sentences.zh: ”北兵先攻武休關，敗都統李顯忠軍，遂入興元，欲衝大安。

translations.literal: " Northern troops first attacked Wuxiu Pass, defeated Commandant Li Xianzhong's army, entered Xingyuan, and intended to strike Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy first attacked Wuxiu Pass, defeated Commandant Li Xianzhong, entered Xingyuan, and aimed at Da'an.

sentences.zh: 製置使趙彥呐檄友聞控製大安以保蜀口。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yan'na ordered Youwen to control Da'an to protect the mouth of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yan'na ordered Youwen to hold Da'an and protect the mouth of Shu.

sentences.zh: 友聞馳書彥呐曰：“沔陽，蜀之險要，吾重兵在此，敵有後顧之憂，必不能越沔陽而入蜀。

translations.literal: Youwen sent a rapid letter to Yan'na: "Mianyang is the strategic point of Shu. With my heavy forces here the enemy will worry about their rear and surely cannot pass Mianyang to enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen wrote urgently to Yan'na: "Mianyang is the strategic key to Shu. With my main force here the enemy will fear for their rear and cannot pass Mianyang into Shu.

sentences.zh: 又有曹萬、王宣首尾應援，可保必捷。

translations.literal: With Cao Wan and Wang Xuan supporting head and tail, victory can be assured.
translations.idiomatic: With Cao Wan and Wang Xuan supporting from front and rear, we can be sure of victory.

sentences.zh: 大安地勢平壙，無險可守，正敵騎所長，步兵所短，況眾寡不敵，豈可於平地控禦。

translations.literal: Da'an's terrain is flat and open with no rugged ground to hold—it favors enemy cavalry and disadvantages infantry; moreover we cannot match their numbers—how can we defend on flat ground?
translations.idiomatic: Da'an is flat and open with nothing to hold. It favors enemy cavalry and not our infantry—and we cannot match their numbers. How can we defend on flat ground?

sentences.zh: ”彥呐不以為然，一日持小紅牌來速者七。

translations.literal: " Yan'na did not agree; in one day seven urgent small red placards arrived.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan'na disagreed. In one day seven urgent red placards arrived.

sentences.zh: 友聞議為以寡擊眾，非乘夜出奇內外夾擊不可。

translations.literal: Youwen judged that to strike the many with the few, nothing would do but a night surprise with inner and outer forces attacking together.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen judged that against such odds only a night surprise with inner and outer forces striking together would work.

sentences.zh: 乃遣萬、友諒引兵上雞冠隘，多張旗幟，示敵堅守。

translations.literal: He therefore sent Wan and Youliang to lead troops up Jiguan Pass with many banners displayed to show the enemy a firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wan and Youliang up Jiguan Pass with many banners to make the enemy think they held firm.

sentences.zh: 友聞選精銳萬人夜渡江，密往流溪設伏。

translations.literal: Youwen selected ten thousand elite troops, crossed the river by night, and secretly went to Liuxi to set an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen chose ten thousand elite men, crossed the river by night, and secretly set an ambush at Liuxi.

sentences.zh: 約曰：“敵至，內以鳴鼓舉火為應，外呼殺聲。

translations.literal: He agreed: "When the enemy comes, those within will answer with drums and fire, those without will shout the kill-cry.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed: "When the enemy comes, those inside signal with drums and fire, those outside shout the kill-cry.

sentences.zh: ”北兵果至，萬出逆戰，敵將八都魯擁萬餘眾，達海帥千人往來搏戰，矢石如雨。

translations.literal: " Northern troops came as expected; Wan went out to meet them. Enemy general Badulu led more than ten thousand; Dahai commanded a thousand going back and forth in battle—arrows and stones like rain.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy came. Wan went out to meet them. Enemy general Badulu led more than ten thousand men. Dahai commanded a thousand in repeated clashes. Arrows and stones fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 萬身被數創，令諸軍舉烽。

translations.literal: Wan received several wounds and ordered the armies to raise beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: Wan took several wounds and ordered the armies to raise beacon fires.

sentences.zh: 友聞遣選鋒軍統製楊大全、遊奕軍統製馮大用引本部出東菜園，擊敵後隊；

translations.literal: Youwen sent Vanguard Commander Yang Daquan and Patrol Commander Feng Dayong with their commands out from East Vegetable Garden to strike the enemy rear;
translations.idiomatic: Youwen sent Vanguard commander Yang Daquan and Patrol commander Feng Dayong from East Vegetable Garden to strike the enemy rear;

sentences.zh: 敢勇軍總管夏用、知西和州神勁軍總管趙興帥所部出水嶺，擊敵中隊；

translations.literal: Dare-Brave Commander Xia Yong and Divine Strength Commander of Xihe Zhao Xing led their commands out from Shuiling to strike the enemy center;
translations.idiomatic: Dare-Brave commander Xia Yong and Divine Strength commander Zhao Xing of Xihe led their men from Shuiling to strike the enemy center;

sentences.zh: 知天水軍安邊軍總管呂嗣德、陳庚率所部出龍泉頭，擊敵前隊。

translations.literal: Frontier Pacification Commander Lü Side of Tianshui Army and Chen Geng led their commands out from Longquantou to strike the enemy vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Pacification commander Lü Side of Tianshui Army and Chen Geng led their men from Longquantou to strike the enemy vanguard.

sentences.zh: 友聞親帥精兵三千人，疾馳至隘下，先遣保捷軍統領劉虎帥敢死士五百人衝前軍，前軍不動，大兵伏三百騎道旁，虎眾銜枚突戰。

translations.literal: Youwen personally led three thousand elite troops racing to the foot of the pass, first sending Valiant Guard Commander Liu Hu with five hundred dare-to-die men to charge the vanguard; the vanguard did not move, but the great army had three hundred cavalry hidden by the road; Hu's men fought with gags in their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen personally led three thousand elite troops to the foot of the pass and first sent Valiant Guard commander Liu Hu with five hundred dare-to-die men against the vanguard. The vanguard held. Three hundred enemy cavalry lay hidden by the road. Hu's men fought with gags in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 會大風雨，諸將請曰：“雨不止，淖濘深沒足，宜俟少霽。

translations.literal: A great wind and rain came; the generals asked: "The rain does not stop and the mud is deep over the feet—we should wait for a brief clearing.
translations.idiomatic: A great storm came. The generals said: "The rain won't stop and the mud is over our ankles—we should wait for it to clear.

sentences.zh: ”友聞斥曰：“敵知我伏兵在此，緩必失機。

translations.literal: " Youwen rebuked them: "The enemy knows our ambush is here—delay will lose the chance.
translations.idiomatic: " Youwen rebuked them: "The enemy knows we are here. Delay will lose our chance.

sentences.zh: ”遂擁兵齊進。

translations.literal: " He then pressed the troops forward together.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed the troops forward together.

sentences.zh: 友聞入龍尾頭，萬聞之，五鼓出隘口，與友聞會。

translations.literal: Youwen entered Longweitou; Wan heard and at the fifth drum sallied from the pass mouth to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen entered Longweitou. Wan heard and at the fifth drum sallied from the pass to join him.

sentences.zh: 內外兩軍皆殊死戰，血流二十里。

translations.literal: The inner and outer armies both fought to the death; blood flowed for twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer forces fought to the death. Blood flowed for twenty li.

sentences.zh: 西軍素以綿裘代鐵甲，經雨濡濕，不利步門。

translations.literal: Western armies habitually used cotton coats in place of iron armor; soaked by rain they were ill-suited for infantry combat.
translations.idiomatic: Western armies used cotton coats instead of iron armor. Soaked by rain they were useless in close fighting.

sentences.zh: 黎明，大兵益增，乃以鐵騎四面圍繞，友聞歎曰：“此殆天乎！

translations.literal: At dawn the great army increased further and surrounded them with iron cavalry on all sides; Youwen sighed: "Is this perhaps heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy host swelled and surrounded them with iron cavalry on all sides. Youwen sighed: "Is this heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 吾有死而已。

translations.literal: I have only death.
translations.idiomatic: I have only death.

sentences.zh: ”於是極口詬罵，殺所乘馬以示必死。

translations.literal: " He then cursed with all his might and killed his mount to show he would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: " He cursed with all his might and killed his horse to show he would not retreat.

sentences.zh: 血戰愈厲，與弟萬俱死，軍盡沒，北兵遂長驅入蜀。

translations.literal: The bloody battle grew fiercer; he and his younger brother Wan both died, the army was entirely destroyed, and northern troops drove straight into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The bloody fight grew fiercer. He and his brother Wan both died. The army was destroyed and northern troops drove straight into Shu.

sentences.zh: 秦鞏人汪世顯素服友聞威望，嚐以名馬遺友聞，還師過戰地，歎曰：“蜀將軍真男兒漢也。

translations.literal: Wang Shixian of Qin-Gong had long respected Youwen's prestige and once gave him a famous horse; returning with his army past the battlefield he sighed: "General of Shu is a true man among men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixian of Qin-Gong had long respected Youwen and once gave him a famous horse. Returning past the battlefield he sighed: "This general of Shu was a true man.

sentences.zh: ”盛禮祭之。

translations.literal: " He offered a grand ritual sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: " He offered a grand sacrifice in his honor.

sentences.zh: 事聞，特贈龍圖閣學士、大中大夫，賜廟褒忠，諡曰毅節，官其二子承務郎，婿迪功郎。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was specially posthumously made academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Grand Master of the Palace, granted the temple Commending Loyalty, given the posthumous title Steadfast Integrity, and two sons were made Gentlemen for Attending to Affairs and his son-in-law Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court he was posthumously made academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Grand Master of the Palace. His temple was named Commending Loyalty and his posthumous title Steadfast Integrity. Two sons received office and his son-in-law was made Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement.

sentences.zh: 萬特贈武翼大夫，二子成忠郎。

translations.literal: Wan was specially posthumously made Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and two sons were made Gentlemen for Accomplished Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was posthumously made Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and two sons were made Gentlemen for Accomplished Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 陳寅，寶謨閣待制鹹之子。

translations.literal: Chen Yin was the son of Xian, a pending appointee of the Baomo Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yin was the son of Xian, a pending appointee of the Baomo Hall.

sentences.zh: 漕司兩貢進士，以父恩補官，曆官州縣。

translations.literal: Twice recommended as jinshi by the transport office, he received office by his father's grace and served in prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Twice recommended as jinshi by the transport office, he received office through his father's privilege and served in prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 紹定初，知西和州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoding he was prefect of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaoding he became prefect of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 西和極邊重地，寅以書生義不辭難。

translations.literal: Xihe was an extreme frontier post; Yin as a scholar in righteousness did not decline the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Xihe was a critical frontier post. Yin, a scholar, did not shrink from the hardship.

sentences.zh: 北兵入境，屬都統何進出守大安，獨統製官王銳與忠義千人城守而已。

translations.literal: When northern troops entered the frontier, Commandant He Jin had gone out to hold Da'an; only Commander Wang Rui and a thousand loyal volunteers remained to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops entered the frontier, Commandant He Jin had gone to hold Da'an. Only Commander Wang Rui and a thousand loyal volunteers remained to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 寅誓與其民共守此土。

translations.literal: Yin swore to defend this land together with his people.
translations.idiomatic: Yin swore to defend this land together with his people.

sentences.zh: 居民始以進留家城中，恃以為固，已而進徙它郡，遂無固誌。

translations.literal: At first the people relied on Jin leaving his family in the city as a pledge of firm defense, but when Jin moved to another prefecture they lost their resolve.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people relied on Jin leaving his family in the city as proof he would hold firm, but when Jin moved elsewhere they lost heart.

sentences.zh: 寅獨留其二子並闔門二十八口，曰：“人各顧其家，將誰共守。

translations.literal: Yin alone kept his two sons and twenty-eight members of his household, saying: "If each man cares only for his own family, who will defend together?
translations.idiomatic: Yin alone kept his two sons and twenty-eight members of his household, saying: "If everyone cares only for his own family, who will defend this place together?

sentences.zh: ”乃散資財以結忠義，為必守之計。

translations.literal: " He then distributed wealth to rally loyal volunteers and made plans for a defense to the death.
translations.idiomatic: " He distributed his wealth to rally loyal volunteers and prepared to hold to the end.

sentences.zh: 北兵十萬攻城東南門，以降者為先驅。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand northern troops attacked the southeast gate with defectors as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand northern troops attacked the southeast gate with defectors in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 寅草檄文喻之，自執旗鼓，激厲將士，迎敵力戰，矢石如雨。

translations.literal: Yin drafted a proclamation to admonish them, himself held banner and drum, roused the officers and soldiers, met the enemy and fought fiercely—arrows and stones like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yin drafted a proclamation to admonish them, took banner and drum himself, roused his men, and met the enemy in fierce fighting. Arrows and stones fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 師退，詰旦，增兵復來，寅帥忠義民兵與敢死士力戰，晝夜數十合，兵退。

translations.literal: The army withdrew; at dawn reinforcements came again; Yin led loyal militia and dare-to-die men in fierce battle through day and night for dozens of clashes before the troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew. At dawn reinforcements returned. Yin led loyal militia and dare-to-die men through dozens of clashes day and night until the enemy withdrew again.

sentences.zh: 製置司以寅功遍告列郡。

translations.literal: The pacification headquarters reported Yin's merit to every prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification headquarters reported Yin's merit to every prefecture.

sentences.zh: 北兵伐木為攻具，增兵至數十萬，圍州城。

translations.literal: Northern troops felled trees for siege engines, increased forces to several hundred thousand, and besieged the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy felled trees for siege engines, raised their host to several hundred thousand, and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 進素與寅不協，寅有功，尤為諸將所忌。

translations.literal: Jin had never been on good terms with Yin; Yin's merit was especially envied by the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had never been on good terms with Yin, and the other generals especially resented Yin's success.

sentences.zh: 至是求援甚急，久之，製置司才遣劉銳及忠義人陳瑀等往救，率皆觀望不進，銳甫進七方關，瑀未及仇池，皆以路梗告。

translations.literal: Now he urgently sought relief; only after a long time did the pacification headquarters send Liu Rui and the loyal volunteer Chen Yu and others to rescue—all mostly held back and did not advance; Rui had just reached Qifang Pass and Yu had not yet reached Chouci when both reported blocked roads.
translations.idiomatic: Relief was urgently needed, but only after a long delay did the pacification headquarters send Liu Rui and loyal volunteer Chen Yu and others. Most held back. Rui had just reached Qifang Pass and Yu had not yet reached Chouci when both reported blocked roads.

sentences.zh: 寅率民兵晝夜苦戰，援兵不至，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Yin led militia in bitter fighting day and night; relief did not come and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yin led militia in bitter fighting day and night. Relief never came and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 寅顧其妻杜氏曰：“若速自為計。

translations.literal: Yin turned to his wife Lady Du: "Make haste to plan for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Yin turned to his wife Lady Du: "Make haste to plan for yourself.

sentences.zh: ”杜厲聲曰：“安有生同君祿，死不共王事者？

translations.literal: " Du said in a stern voice: "How could there be one who shares her husband's salary in life but not the king's service in death?
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Du said sharply: "How could I share your salary in life but not the king's service in death?

sentences.zh: ”即登高堡自飲藥。

translations.literal: " She at once ascended the high fort and drank poison.
translations.idiomatic: " She climbed the high fort and drank poison.

sentences.zh: 二子及婦俱死母傍。

translations.literal: Her two sons and daughters-in-law all died beside their mother.
translations.idiomatic: Her two sons and daughters-in-law died beside her.

sentences.zh: 寅斂而焚之，乃朝服登戰樓，望闕焚香，號泣曰：“臣始謀守此城，為蜀藩籬，城之不存，臣死分也。

translations.literal: Yin gathered and burned them, then in court dress ascended the battle tower, faced the palace gate to burn incense, and wailed: "Your servant first planned to hold this city as a screen for Shu; if the city does not stand, your servant's death is his portion.
translations.idiomatic: Yin gathered and burned them, then in court dress climbed the battle tower, faced the palace gate to burn incense, and wept: "I planned to hold this city as a screen for Shu. If the city falls, my death is only my due.

sentences.zh: 臣不負國！

translations.literal: Your servant has not failed the state!
translations.idiomatic: I have not failed the state!

sentences.zh: 臣不負國！

translations.literal: Your servant has not failed the state!
translations.idiomatic: I have not failed the state!

sentences.zh: ”再拜伏劍而死。

translations.literal: " He bowed twice and fell on his sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed twice and fell on his sword.

sentences.zh: 賓客同死者二十有八人。

translations.literal: Twenty-eight guests died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eight guests died with him.

sentences.zh: 一子後至，亦欲自裁，軍士抱持之曰：“不可使忠臣無後。

translations.literal: One son arrived later and also wished to kill himself; soldiers held him and said: "We cannot let a loyal minister have no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: One son arrived later and also wished to kill himself. Soldiers held him and said: "We cannot let a loyal minister leave no descendants.

sentences.zh: ”與俱縋城，亦折足死。

translations.literal: " They lowered him from the wall together and he also died with broken legs.
translations.idiomatic: " They lowered him from the wall with them, and he too died with broken legs.

sentences.zh: 製置司以聞，詔特贈朝議大夫、右文殿修撰，賜錢三千緡，即其所居鄉、所守州立廟。

translations.literal: The pacification headquarters reported it; an edict specially posthumously made him Grand Master for Discussion of Policy and compiler at the Hall of Literary Glory on the Right, granted three thousand strings of cash, and ordered temples built in his home village and the prefecture he had held.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification headquarters reported his death. The court posthumously made him Grand Master for Discussion of Policy and compiler at the Hall of Literary Glory on the Right, granted three thousand strings of cash, and ordered temples built in his home village and in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 久之，加贈華文閣待制，諡襄節。

translations.literal: After a long time he was further posthumously made pending appointee of the Huawen Hall with the posthumous title Assisting Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further posthumously made pending appointee of the Huawen Hall with the posthumous title Assisting Integrity.

sentences.zh: 賈子坤字伯厚，潼川懷安軍人。

translations.literal: Jia Zikun, styled Bohou, was a native of Huai'an Army in Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zikun, styled Bohou, was from Huai'an Army in Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Jiading.

sentences.zh: 為西和推官，攝通判。

translations.literal: He was investigating officer of Xihe and acted as vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was investigating officer of Xihe and acted as vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 關外被兵，子坤與郡守陳寅誓死城守。

translations.literal: When the outer passes suffered attack, Zikun and the prefect Chen Yin swore to die defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the outer passes came under attack, Zikun and prefect Chen Yin swore to die defending the city.

sentences.zh: 城陷，子坤朝服與其家十二口死之。

translations.literal: When the city fell Zikun in court dress died together with twelve members of his household.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Zikun in court dress died with twelve members of his household.

sentences.zh: 追贈承議郎，封其父崧承務郎。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and his father Song was enfeoffed as Gentleman for Attending to Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and his father Song was enfeoffed as Gentleman for Attending to Affairs.

sentences.zh: 官其子仲武宣教郎、隆州簽判，改奉議郎、果州通判，卒。

translations.literal: His son Zhongwu was given office as Gentleman for Instruction and signing officer of Longzhou, changed to Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and vice prefect of Guozhou, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongwu received office as Gentleman for Instruction and signing officer of Longzhou, later became Gentleman for Discussion of Policy and vice prefect of Guozhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 仲武子昌忠、純孝，同登鹹淳七年進士第。

translations.literal: Zhongwu's sons Changzhong and Chunxiao both passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Xianchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu's sons Changzhong and Chunxiao both passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Xianchun.

sentences.zh: 純孝揚州教授，受知帥李庭芝，調江、淮總幕。

translations.literal: Chunxiao was professor at Yangzhou, won the favor of commander Li Tingzhi, and was transferred to the Jiang-Huai general staff.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxiao was professor at Yangzhou, won favor with commander Li Tingzhi, and joined the Jiang-Huai general staff.

sentences.zh: 北兵下江南，二王在福州，以史館檢閱召，辭。

translations.literal: When northern troops descended on Jiangnan the two princes were at Fuzhou and summoned him as archival reviewer; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops swept into Jiangnan the two princes were at Fuzhou and summoned him as archival reviewer. He declined.

sentences.zh: 會丞相文天祥辟佐其幕，尋授秘書丞，擢吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Wen Tianxiang invited him to his staff he soon received office as secretary and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wen Tianxiang then invited him to his staff. He soon became secretary and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復為右司，轉朝散郎。

translations.literal: Mourning his mother, he was recalled from mourning to the Right Office and transferred to Gentleman for Scattered Service.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was recalled to the Right Office and made Gentleman for Scattered Service.

sentences.zh: 崖山師敗，純孝抱二女偕妻牟同蹈海死。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at Yamen, Chunxiao embraced his two daughters and with his wife Mou together drowned in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was defeated at Yamen, Chunxiao embraced his two daughters and drowned in the sea with his wife Mou.

sentences.zh: 汝曏宣城人，善射。

translations.literal: Ru Xiang of Xuancheng was skilled in archery.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Xiang of Xuancheng was skilled in archery.

sentences.zh: 城破被執，先斷其兩臂，而後臠殺之。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was captured; first both arms were cut off, then he was dismembered and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was captured, both arms were cut off first, then he was dismembered and killed.

sentences.zh: 銳及其二子自刎死，軍民死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Rui and his two sons killed themselves by cutting their throats; soldiers and civilians who died numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and his two sons cut their throats. Tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians died.

sentences.zh: 蹇彝，潼川通泉人。

translations.literal: Jian Yi was a native of Tongquan in Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi was from Tongquan in Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jiading.

sentences.zh: 累官通判金州。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to vice prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through offices to vice prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，北兵攻蜀，彝堅守，戰不能敵，被擒，不屈而死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping northern troops attacked Shu; Yi held firm, could not match them in battle, was captured, and died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duanping northern troops attacked Shu. Yi held firm, could not match them in battle, was captured, and died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 其子永叔復力戰，城破，舉家死焉。

translations.literal: His son Yongshu again fought fiercely; when the city fell the whole family died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongshu fought on fiercely. When the city fell the whole family died.

sentences.zh: 弟維之，紹定五年進士。

translations.literal: His younger brother Weizhi was a jinshi of the fifth year of Shaoding.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Weizhi passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Shaoding.

sentences.zh: 利州都統王宣辟行參軍事，亦迎敵力戰而死，特官其子。

translations.literal: Lizhou commandant Wang Xuan invited him as traveling staff officer; he also met the enemy and died fighting fiercely; his son was specially granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou commandant Wang Xuan invited him as staff officer. He too met the enemy and died fighting. His son was specially granted office.

sentences.zh: 何充，漢州德陽人。

translations.literal: He Chong was a native of Deyang in Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong was from Deyang in Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 秘書監耕之孫。

translations.literal: He was the grandson of Gengzhi, director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Gengzhi, director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 通判黎州，攝州事，預為備禦計。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Lizhou he acted in prefectural affairs and made plans for defense in advance.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of Lizhou he acted in prefectural affairs and prepared defenses in advance.

sentences.zh: 及宋能之至，建議急於邛崍創大小兩關倉及砦屋百間，親督程役。

translations.literal: When Song Nengzhi arrived he urged urgently creating large and small pass granaries and a hundred fort buildings at Qionglai and personally supervised the labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Nengzhi arrived he urged building large and small pass granaries and a hundred fort buildings at Qionglai and personally supervised the work.

sentences.zh: 俄關破，充自刺不死，大軍帥呼之語，許以不殺。

translations.literal: Soon the pass fell; Chong stabbed himself but did not die; the army commander called to speak with him and promised not to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the pass fell. Chong stabbed himself but did not die. The army commander called to him and promised not to kill him.

sentences.zh: 充曰：“吾三世食趙氏祿，為趙氏死不憾。

translations.literal: Chong said: "For three generations my family has eaten the Zhao house's salary—to die for the Zhao house I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said: "For three generations my family has eaten the Zhao house's salary. To die for the Zhao house I have no regret.

sentences.zh: ”帥設帟幄環坐諸將，而虛其賓席，呼充曰：“汝能降，即坐此。

translations.literal: " The commander set up curtains with generals seated in a ring and left the guest seat empty, calling to Chong: "If you can submit, sit here.
translations.idiomatic: " The commander set up curtains with his generals seated in a ring and left the guest seat empty. He called to Chong: "If you will submit, sit here.

sentences.zh: ”充踞坐地求死，遂罷。

translations.literal: " Chong sat on the ground asking for death and they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong sat on the ground demanding death, and they desisted.

sentences.zh: 它日又呼之，欲辮其發而髡其頂。

translations.literal: Another day they called him again, intending to braid his hair and shave his crown.
translations.idiomatic: Another day they called him again, intending to braid his hair and shave his crown.

sentences.zh: 曰：“可殺不可髡。

translations.literal: He said: "You may kill me but you may not shave me.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "You may kill me, but you may not shave me.

sentences.zh: ”又使署招民榜，充曰：“吾監州也，可聚吾民使殺之耶？

translations.literal: " They also made him sign a placard to summon the people; Chong said: "I supervise this prefecture—would you gather my people to have them killed?
translations.idiomatic: " They also made him sign a placard summoning the people. Chong said: "I govern this prefecture—would you gather my people to have them killed?

sentences.zh: 即一家有死而已，榜必不可署。

translations.literal: At most one household would die—that placard I absolutely cannot sign.
translations.idiomatic: At most one household would die. That placard I will never sign.

sentences.zh: ”大將遺以酒茗羊牛肉，皆卻之。

translations.literal: " The general sent him wine, tea, mutton, and beef—all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: " The general sent wine, tea, mutton, and beef—all were refused.

sentences.zh: 自是水飲絕不入口。

translations.literal: From then on he would not let a drop of water pass his lips.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he took no water at all.

sentences.zh: 敵知其不可強，將剮之，大將曰：“此南家好漢也，使之即死。

translations.literal: The enemy knew he could not be forced and was about to dismember him; the general said: "This is a true man of the south—let him die at once.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy knew he could not be broken and was about to dismember him. The general said: "This is a true man of the south—let him die at once.

sentences.zh: ”於是斬其首。

translations.literal: " His head was then cut off.
translations.idiomatic: " His head was cut off.

sentences.zh: 充妻陳罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Chong's wife Chen cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's wife Chen cursed without stop.

sentences.zh: 初，充之見呼也，陳必以一家往。

translations.literal: When Chong was first summoned, Chen always went with the whole family.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong was first summoned, Chen always went with the whole family.

sentences.zh: 帥曰：“不呼汝，何以來？

translations.literal: The commander said: "If we did not summon you, why did you come?
translations.idiomatic: The commander said: "If we did not summon you, why did you come?

sentences.zh: ”陳曰：“吾求死爾。

translations.literal: " Chen said: "I came seeking death, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen said: "I came seeking death, that is all.

sentences.zh: ”及充死，東望再拜曰：“臣夫婦雖死，可以對趙氏無愧矣。

translations.literal: " When Chong died she bowed twice toward the east and said: "Though we husband and wife die, we can face the Zhao house without shame.
translations.idiomatic: " When Chong died she bowed twice toward the east and said: "Though we husband and wife die, we can face the Zhao house without shame.

sentences.zh: ”眾以石擊殺之。

translations.literal: " The crowd stoned her to death.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd stoned her to death.

sentences.zh: 方充夫婦之嬰禍也，親戚勸其苟免，充正色曰：“我夫婦與兒婦義同死，汝等自求生可也。

translations.literal: When Chong and his wife met disaster, relatives urged them to save themselves somehow; Chong said with stern countenance: "We husband and wife share death with our daughters-in-law in righteousness—you may seek life for yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck, relatives urged them to save themselves. Chong said sternly: "We husband and wife will die with our daughters-in-law in righteousness—you may save yourselves.

sentences.zh: ”於是上下感泣，願同死者四十餘人。

translations.literal: " High and low were moved to tears; more than forty wished to die with them.
translations.idiomatic: " High and low wept; more than forty wished to die with them.

sentences.zh: 男士麟、孫駒行、從子仲桂先充而死，惟長子士龍得免。

translations.literal: The men Shilin, Sun Juxing, and nephew Zhonggui died before Chong; only the eldest son Shilong escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin, Sun Juxing, and nephew Zhonggui died before Chong. Only his eldest son Shilong escaped.

sentences.zh: 許彪孫，顯謨閣學士奕之子也。

translations.literal: Xu Biaosun was the son of Yi, academician of the Xianmo Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Biaosun was the son of Yi, academician of the Xianmo Hall.

sentences.zh: 為四川製置司參謀官。

translations.literal: He was staff officer of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 景定二年，劉整叛，召彪孫草降文，以潼川一道為獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingding Liu Zheng rebelled and summoned Biaosun to draft a surrender document offering the whole Tongchuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingding Liu Zheng rebelled and summoned Biaosun to draft a surrender offering the whole Tongchuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 彪孫辭使者曰：“此腕可斷，此筆不可書也。

translations.literal: Biaosun told the envoy: "This wrist may be cut off, but this brush cannot write.
translations.idiomatic: Biaosun told the envoy: "This wrist may be cut off, but this brush will not write.

sentences.zh: ”即閉門與家人俱仰藥死。

translations.literal: " He shut his doors and with his family all drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He shut his doors and he and his family drank poison together.

sentences.zh: 又有史季儉者，威州棋城主簿也。

translations.literal: There was also Shi Jijian, recorder of Qicheng in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Shi Jijian, recorder of Qicheng in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 成都之陷，子良震與婿楊城夫爭相為死，各特贈兩官，與一子下州文學。

translations.literal: When Chengdu fell, Zi Liangzhen and his son-in-law Yang Chengfu vied to die for the state; each was specially posthumously given two ranks and one son was made literary officer of a lower prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu fell, Zi Liangzhen and his son-in-law Yang Chengfu vied to die for the state. Each was posthumously given two ranks and one son was made literary officer of a lower prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，製置使丁黼辟為參議官，先遣其家歸鄉里，為文訣先墓，誓以身死報國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi Pacification Commissioner Ding Fu invited him as deliberation officer, first sent his family home, wrote a farewell at his ancestors' tombs, and swore to repay the state with his death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaxi Pacification Commissioner Ding Fu invited Wang Yi as deliberation officer. Yi first sent his family home, wrote a farewell at his ancestors' tombs, and swore to repay the state with his life.

sentences.zh: 及北兵至，帳前提舉官成駒先走，黼倉卒迎敵，敗死。

translations.literal: When northern troops arrived, headquarters promoter Cheng Ju fled first; Fu hastily met the enemy and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops arrived, headquarters promoter Cheng Ju fled first. Fu met the enemy in haste and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 翊與司理王璨、運司幹官李日宣等募兵拒守。

translations.literal: Yi with judicial officer Wang Can, transport handler Li Rixuan, and others recruited troops to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Yi with judicial officer Wang Can, transport handler Li Rixuan, and others recruited troops to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 兵入公署，見翊朝服危坐，問為何人，曰：“小官食天子之祿，臨難不能救，死有餘罪，可速殺我。

translations.literal: Troops entered the government office, saw Yi in court dress sitting upright, and asked who he was; he said: "This petty officer eats the Son of Heaven's salary; facing crisis he could not save the city—death leaves guilt enough; kill me quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Troops entered the government office and found Yi in court dress sitting upright. Asked who he was, he said: "I eat the emperor's salary. Facing this crisis I could not save the city—death is my due. Kill me quickly.

sentences.zh: ”又問何以不走，曰：“願與此城俱亡。

translations.literal: " Asked why he did not flee, he said: "I wish to perish with this city.
translations.idiomatic: " Asked why he did not flee, he said: "I wish to perish with this city.

sentences.zh: ”北兵相謂曰：“忠臣也。

translations.literal: " The northern soldiers said to one another: "A loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: " The northern soldiers said to one another: "A loyal minister.

sentences.zh: ”戒勿殺。

translations.literal: " They warned one another not to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: " They warned one another not to kill him.

sentences.zh: 敵縱火大掠，翊以朝服赴井死。

translations.literal: The enemy set fires and plundered greatly; Yi in court dress threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy set fires and plundered. Yi in court dress threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 兵後，其家出其屍井中，衣冠儼如也。

translations.literal: After the troops withdrew his family drew his corpse from the well; cap and robes were still dignified.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops withdrew his family drew his body from the well. His cap and robes were still dignified.

sentences.zh: 轉運副使蒲東卯死之。

translations.literal: Transport Vice Commissioner Pu Dongmao died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Transport vice commissioner Pu Dongmao also died.

sentences.zh: 兵屠漢州，權州事劉當可、判官邵復、錄事參軍羅由、司戶參軍趙崇啟、知雒縣羅君文皆不屈而死。

translations.literal: When troops massacred Hanzhou, acting prefect Liu Dangke, vice magistrate Shao Fu, recording officer Luo You, revenue officer Zhao Chongqi, and Luoxian magistrate Luo Junwen all died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: When troops massacred Hanzhou, acting prefect Liu Dangke, vice magistrate Shao Fu, recording officer Luo You, revenue officer Zhao Chongqi, and Luoxian magistrate Luo Junwen all died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 復，雍六世孫也。

translations.literal: Fu was a sixth-generation descendant of the Yong clan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was a sixth-generation descendant of the Yong clan.

sentences.zh: 入眉州，知丹棱縣馮仲燁死之。

translations.literal: Entering Meizhou, Danleng magistrate Feng Zhongye died.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Meizhou, Danleng magistrate Feng Zhongye died.

sentences.zh: 取簡州，簡守李大全死之。

translations.literal: Taking Jianzhou, Jian prefect Li Daquan died.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Jianzhou, Jian prefect Li Daquan died.

sentences.zh: 邛守趙晨親率雅州牌手出戰，力盡而死。

translations.literal: Qiong prefect Zhao Chen personally led Yazhou shield-bearers out to battle and died when his strength was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong prefect Zhao Chen personally led Yazhou shield-bearers into battle and died when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 文州守劉銳、通判趙汝曏相誓死守，更迭出戰，被圍旬有五日，汲道絕，兵民水不入口者半月，至吮妻子之血，卒無叛誌。

translations.literal: Wenzhou prefect Liu Rui and vice prefect Zhao Ruxiang swore to die defending together, taking turns going out to fight; besieged for fifteen days, water routes cut off, soldiers and people went half a month without water, even sucking their wives' and children's blood, yet in the end none wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhou prefect Liu Rui and vice prefect Zhao Ruxiang swore to die defending together and took turns fighting. Besieged for fifteen days with water cut off, soldiers and civilians went half a month without drinking—even sucking their wives' and children's blood—yet none wavered.

sentences.zh: 城垂陷，汝曏猶提雙刃入陣，中十六矢，被執以死。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall Ruxiang still took twin blades into the battle line, was struck by sixteen arrows, captured, and killed.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall Ruxiang still charged into the line with twin blades, took sixteen arrows, was captured, and killed.

sentences.zh: 銳先殺其妻，父子三人登文王台自刎死。

translations.literal: Rui first killed his wife; father and two sons ascended King Wen's Terrace and killed themselves by cutting their throats.
translations.idiomatic: Rui first killed his wife. Father and two sons climbed King Wen's Terrace and cut their throats.

sentences.zh: 師至遂寧，民兵趙朋拒戰，左臂已斷，而戰不休。

translations.literal: When the army reached Suining, militiaman Zhao Peng resisted; his left arm was already severed yet he did not stop fighting.
translations.idiomatic: At Suining militiaman Zhao Peng resisted. His left arm was already severed yet he would not stop fighting.

sentences.zh: 至重慶，進士胡天啟負母而逃，兵欲殺其母，天啟妻張哀號願以身代，不聽，卒殺之。

translations.literal: At Chongqing, jinshi Hu Tianqi fled carrying his mother; soldiers wished to kill his mother; Tianqi's wife Zhang wailed and begged to take her place—they would not listen and finally killed her.
translations.idiomatic: At Chongqing jinshi Hu Tianqi fled carrying his mother. Soldiers meant to kill her. His wife Zhang wailed and begged to take her place. They refused and killed her.

sentences.zh: 天啟與其妻呼天大罵，大將奇天啟貌，欲活之，謂之曰：“汝從我，當共富貴。

translations.literal: Tianqi and his wife cried to heaven and cursed loudly; the general marveled at Tianqi's appearance and wished to spare him, saying: "Follow me and we shall share wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi and his wife cried to heaven and cursed. The general marveled at Tianqi's looks and wished to spare him, saying: "Follow me and we shall share wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: ”天啟愈奮罵，於是夫婦同死。

translations.literal: " Tianqi cursed all the more fiercely, and husband and wife died together.
translations.idiomatic: " Tianqi cursed all the more fiercely. Husband and wife died together.

sentences.zh: 事聞，翊、汝曏皆立廟賜諡，餘褒恤有差。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, temples and posthumous titles were granted to Yi and Ruxiang; the rest received differentiated honors and relief.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, temples and posthumous titles were granted to Yi and Ruxiang; the rest received honors and relief according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 寶祐六年，北兵拔吉平隘，守將楊禮、周德榮死之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Baoyou northern troops took Jiping Pass; garrison commanders Yang Li and Zhou Derong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Baoyou northern troops took Jiping Pass. Garrison commanders Yang Li and Zhou Derong died.

sentences.zh: 拔長寧，守將王佐父子俱死。

translations.literal: Taking Changning, garrison commander Wang Zuo and his son both died.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Changning, garrison commander Wang Zuo and his son both died.

sentences.zh: 至閬州，推官趙廣死之。

translations.literal: Reaching Langzhou, investigating officer Zhao Guang died.
translations.idiomatic: At Langzhou investigating officer Zhao Guang died.

sentences.zh: 至蓬州，轉運使施擇善死之。

translations.literal: Reaching Pengzhou, transport commissioner Shi Zeshan died.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengzhou transport commissioner Shi Zeshan died.

sentences.zh: 至順慶，帥守段元鑒城守，麾下劉淵殺之以降。

translations.literal: Reaching Shunqing, commander Duan Yuanjian defended the city; his subordinate Liu Yuan killed him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Shunqing commander Duan Yuanjian defended the city. His subordinate Liu Yuan killed him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 李誠之字茂欽，婺州東陽人。

translations.literal: Li Chengzhi, styled Maoqin, was a native of Dongyang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengzhi, styled Maoqin, was from Dongyang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 受學呂祖謙。

translations.literal: He studied under Lü Zuqian.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Lü Zuqian.

sentences.zh: 鄉舉第一，後入太學，舍選亦第一。

translations.literal: First in the provincial examination, later entering the Metropolitan University he was also first in dormitory selection.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the provincial examination and later ranked first in dormitory selection at the Metropolitan University.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，釋褐為饒州教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan he left the russet robe to become professor at Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qingyuan he entered office as professor at Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁父母憂，廬墓終喪。

translations.literal: Mourning his parents, he kept vigil at their tombs through the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his parents, he kept vigil at their tombs through the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 幹辦福建安撫司公事，遷刑、工部架閣，擢國子學錄，以言罷。

translations.literal: He was handler in the Fujian Pacification Commission, transferred to archivist in the Ministries of Justice and Works, promoted to recorder of the Imperial University, and was dismissed for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as handler in the Fujian Pacification Commission, became archivist in the ministries of Justice and Works, was promoted to recorder of the Imperial University, and was dismissed after remonstrating.

sentences.zh: 起為江西轉運司幹辦。

translations.literal: He was recalled as handler in the Jiangxi Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as handler in the Jiangxi Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 使稱提會子，第其物力高下輸錢以斂之，誠之以為擾。

translations.literal: The commissioner promoted huizi notes, ranking property high and low to collect money thereby; Chengzhi considered it a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner promoted huizi notes, ranking property to collect money thereby. Chengzhi considered it a disturbance.

sentences.zh: 使者不悅曰：“商君之令，猶能必行，今乃齟齬如此。

translations.literal: The commissioner said displeased: "Lord Shang's orders could still be enforced—yet now there is such friction.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner said displeased: "Lord Shang's orders could still be enforced—yet now there is such friction.

sentences.zh: ”誠之愀然曰：“使君儒者，而欲效商君之所為乎？

translations.literal: " Chengzhi said somberly: "Commissioner, you are a Confucian—do you wish to imitate what Lord Shang did?
translations.idiomatic: " Chengzhi said somberly: "Commissioner, you are a Confucian—do you wish to imitate Lord Shang?

sentences.zh: ”遂辭去。

translations.literal: " He then resigned and left.
translations.idiomatic: " He resigned and left.

sentences.zh: 使者遜謝，罷令而後止。

translations.literal: The commissioner apologized humbly and withdrew the order before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner apologized and withdrew the order.

sentences.zh: 改通判常州，知郢州。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice prefect of Changzhou and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice prefect of Changzhou and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 知金人必敗盟，大修邊防戰攻守禦之具。

translations.literal: Knowing the Jurchens would surely break the treaty, he greatly repaired frontier defenses and equipment for attack, defense, and guarding.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Jurchens would break the treaty, he greatly strengthened frontier defenses and equipment for attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 移知蘄州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 蘄自南渡以來，未嚐被兵，誠之曰：“備禦無素，長驅而來，將若之何？

translations.literal: Qizhou since the southern crossing had never suffered attack; Chengzhi said: "Defense has not been prepared—if they drive straight in, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Qizhou had not been attacked since the southern crossing. Chengzhi said: "We are unprepared—if they drive straight in, what then?

sentences.zh: ”相視城壁而增益之，備樓櫓，築羊馬牆，教閱廂禁民兵，激之以賞，積粟四萬。

translations.literal: " He inspected the walls and strengthened them, prepared towers and rams, built cavalry barriers, drilled ward militia, spurred them with rewards, and stored forty thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: " He inspected the walls and strengthened them, prepared towers, built cavalry barriers, drilled ward militia, spurred them with rewards, and stored forty thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 先是，酒庫月解錢四百五十千以獻守，誠之一無所受，寄諸公帑，以助兵食。

translations.literal: Earlier the wine depot monthly submitted four hundred fifty thousand cash to the prefect; Chengzhi accepted none of it and placed it in the public treasury to aid military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the wine depot monthly submitted four hundred fifty thousand cash to the prefect. Chengzhi accepted none and placed it in the public treasury for military provisions.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年二月，金人犯淮南。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year of Jiading the Jurchens invaded Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourteenth year of Jiading the Jurchens invaded Huainan.

sentences.zh: 時誠之已逾滿，代者不至，欲先遣其孥歸，聞難作而止。

translations.literal: Chengzhi's term had already expired and his replacement had not arrived; he wished first to send his family home but stopped on hearing trouble had begun.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi's term had expired and his replacement had not arrived. He wished to send his family home first but stopped when trouble began.

sentences.zh: 喟然謂其僚曰：“吾以書生再任邊壘，行年七十，抑又何求，獨欠一死爾。

translations.literal: He sighed to his staff: "I as a scholar serve twice on the frontier; I am seventy years old—what more could I seek? Only one death remains owed.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed to his staff: "I am a scholar serving twice on the frontier at seventy years old—what more could I want? Only death remains.

sentences.zh: 當與同僚戮力以守，不濟則以死繼之。

translations.literal: We must strive together with our colleagues to defend; if we fail, let death follow.
translations.idiomatic: We must strive together to defend. If we fail, let death follow.

sentences.zh: ”乃選丁壯分布城守，募死士迎擊，遇於橫槎橋，大破之。

translations.literal: " He selected able-bodied men to distribute for city defense, recruited dare-to-die men to meet the attack, encountered them at Hengchao Bridge, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " He posted able-bodied men around the walls, recruited dare-to-die men, met the enemy at Hengchao Bridge, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 居數日，金人擁眾臨沙河，欲渡，又破之。

translations.literal: After several days the Jurchens massed at Shahe intending to cross and were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the Jurchens massed at Shahe intending to cross and were defeated again.

sentences.zh: 明日，金兵大至，決湟水，焚戰樓，又拒退之。

translations.literal: The next day Jurchen troops came in force, breached the Huang River, burned the battle towers, and were repelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jurchen troops came in force, breached the Huang River, burned the battle towers, and were repelled again.

sentences.zh: 明日，金移兵要衝，為必渡計，蘄兵直前奮擊，殺其酋帥。

translations.literal: The next day the Jurchens shifted troops to a vital crossing intending certain passage; Qizhou troops charged straight ahead fiercely and killed their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Jurchens shifted to a vital crossing. Qizhou troops charged forward and killed their chieftain.

sentences.zh: 金人雖屢挫，然謀益巧，攻益力。

translations.literal: Though the Jurchens were repeatedly defeated, their plans grew more cunning and their attacks more forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly defeated, the Jurchens grew more cunning and pressed harder.

sentences.zh: 未幾，傅城下，圍之數重，遂燔木柵。

translations.literal: Before long they pressed to the foot of the walls, surrounded it in many rings, and burned the wooden palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they pressed the walls, surrounded the city in many rings, and burned the wooden palisade.

sentences.zh: 誠之出兵禦之，又殺其將卒數十人，奪所佩印。

translations.literal: Chengzhi led troops out to resist, killed several dozen of their officers and soldiers, and seized the seal one wore.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi led troops out, killed dozens of their officers and men, and seized a commander's seal.

sentences.zh: 三月朔，金人攻西門，射卻之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month the Jurchens attacked the west gate and were driven back by arrows.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month the Jurchens attacked the west gate and were driven back.

sentences.zh: 俄造望樓以窺城，誠之為疑兵以示之。

translations.literal: Soon they built observation towers to spy on the city; Chengzhi displayed deception troops to show them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they built observation towers to spy on the city. Chengzhi displayed decoy troops.

sentences.zh: 又使持書來脅降，誠之戮之，而還其書。

translations.literal: They also sent someone with a letter threatening surrender; Chengzhi executed him and returned the letter.
translations.idiomatic: They sent a messenger threatening surrender. Chengzhi executed him and returned the letter.

sentences.zh: 越二日，金人以攻具進，誠之設械禦之，夜出搗其營。

translations.literal: Two days later the Jurchens advanced siege engines; Chengzhi set devices to resist and by night raided their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the Jurchens advanced siege engines. Chengzhi set devices to resist and raided their camp by night.

sentences.zh: 料敵應變若熟知兵者，金人卒不得誌。

translations.literal: Anticipating the enemy and adapting as if thoroughly versed in war, the Jurchens in the end could not achieve their aim.
translations.idiomatic: Anticipating the enemy and adapting like a seasoned commander, he kept the Jurchens from their aim.

sentences.zh: 會黃州失守，並兵為一，凡十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Huangzhou fell their forces united into one host of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangzhou fell their forces united into one host of more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 池陽、合肥援兵敗走，朝命馮榯援二郡，榯至境，遷延不進。

translations.literal: Relief troops from Chiyang and Hefei were defeated and fled; the court ordered Feng Zhen to aid the two prefectures, but Zhen reached the border and delayed without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Relief from Chiyang and Hefei was defeated and fled. The court ordered Feng Zhen to aid both prefectures, but he reached the border and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 誠之激厲將士，勉以忠義。

translations.literal: Chengzhi roused the officers and soldiers and exhorted them with loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi roused his officers and soldiers and exhorted them with loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 城陷，率兵巷戰，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: When the city fell he led troops in alley fighting; kills and wounds were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he led troops in street fighting. Casualties were heavy on both sides.

sentences.zh: 子士允力戰死，誠之引劍將自剄，呼其孥曰：“城已破，汝等宜速死，無辱！

translations.literal: His son Shiyun died fighting fiercely; Chengzhi drew his sword to cut his throat and called to his family: "The city is broken—you should die quickly, without disgrace!
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyun died fighting. Chengzhi drew his sword to cut his throat and called to his family: "The city is fallen—you should die quickly, without disgrace!

sentences.zh: ”妻許及婦若孫皆赴水死。

translations.literal: " His wife Xu and daughters-in-law and grandsons all drowned in the water.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife Xu, daughters-in-law, and grandsons all drowned.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈朝散大夫、秘閣修撰，封正節侯，立廟於蘄，賜名褒忠，賻銀絹二百，仍賜爵迪功郎者三，贈其妻令人，士允通直郎，子婦及孫女之沒於難者皆贈安人。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was posthumously made Gentleman for Scattered Service and compiler at the Secretariat Archive, enfeoffed as Marquis of Upright Integrity, a temple was built at Qizhou named Commending Loyalty, two hundred strings of silver and silk were granted for funeral expenses, three were given the rank Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement, his wife was made Lady, Shiyun was made Regular Attendant, and daughters-in-law and granddaughters who perished in the disaster were all made Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Gentleman for Scattered Service and compiler at the Secretariat Archive, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Upright Integrity, and built a temple at Qizhou named Commending Loyalty. Two hundred strings of silver and silk were granted for funeral expenses. Three descendants received the rank Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement. His wife was made Lady, Shiyun Regular Attendant, and daughters-in-law and granddaughters who perished were all made Ladies.

sentences.zh: 從誠之之死者，通判州事秦钜。

translations.literal: Those who died with Chengzhi included vice prefect Qin Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with Chengzhi included vice prefect Qin Ju.

sentences.zh: 秦钜字子野，丞相檜曾孫。

translations.literal: Qin Ju, styled Ziye, was a great-grandson of Chancellor Qin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ju, styled Ziye, was a great-grandson of Chancellor Qin Hui.

sentences.zh: 通判蘄州。

translations.literal: He was vice prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 金人犯境，與郡守李誠之協力捍禦。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded the prefecture he joined prefect Li Chengzhi in strenuous defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded he joined prefect Li Chengzhi in defending the city.

sentences.zh: 求援於武昌、安慶，月餘，兵不至。

translations.literal: They sought relief from Wuchang and Anqing; for more than a month troops did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: They sought relief from Wuchang and Anqing, but for more than a month no troops came.

sentences.zh: 策應兵徐揮、常用等棄城遁。

translations.literal: Relief troops under Xu Hui, Chang Yong, and others abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops under Xu Hui, Chang Yong, and others abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 城破，钜與誠之各以自隨之兵巷戰，死傷略盡。

translations.literal: When the city fell Ju and Chengzhi each fought in the alleys with the troops they had brought; dead and wounded were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Ju and Chengzhi each fought in the streets with their own troops until nearly all were dead or wounded.

sentences.zh: 钜歸署，疾呼吏人劉迪，令火諸倉庫，乃赴一室自焚。

translations.literal: Ju returned to his office, urgently called clerk Liu Di, ordered all storehouses fired, and went to a room to burn himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ju returned to his office, urgently called clerk Liu Di, ordered all storehouses set afire, and went to a room to burn himself.

sentences.zh: 有老卒見煙焰中著白戰袍者，識其钜也，冒火挽出之。

translations.literal: An old soldier saw someone in a white battle robe in the flames, recognized Ju, and braved the fire to pull him out.
translations.idiomatic: An old soldier saw someone in a white battle robe in the flames, recognized Ju, and braved the fire to pull him out.

sentences.zh: 钜叱曰：“我為國死，汝輩可自求生。

translations.literal: Ju rebuked him: "I die for the state—you may seek life for yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ju rebuked him: "I die for the state—you may save yourselves.

sentences.zh: ”製衣就焚而死。

translations.literal: " He put on his robes and burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: " He dressed properly and burned to death.

sentences.zh: 次子浚先往四祖山，兵至亟還，與弟瀈從父俱死。

translations.literal: His second son Jun had first gone to Mount Sizu; when troops came he hurried back and died together with his younger brother Hui and his father.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jun had gone to Mount Sizu first. When troops came he hurried back and died with his younger brother Hui and his father.

sentences.zh: 特贈钜五官、秘閣修撰，封義烈侯，與誠之皆立廟蘄州，賜額褒忠，贈浚、瀈通直郎，賻以銀絹各二百。

translations.literal: Ju was specially posthumously advanced five ranks and made compiler at the Secretariat Archive, enfeoffed as Marquis of Righteous Fervor; temples were built for him and Chengzhi at Qizhou with the plaque Commending Loyalty; Jun and Hui were made Regular Attendants; two hundred strings of silver and silk each were granted for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was posthumously advanced five ranks and made compiler at the Secretariat Archive, enfeoffed as Marquis of Righteous Fervor. Temples were built for him and Chengzhi at Qizhou with the plaque Commending Loyalty. Jun and Hui were made Regular Attendants. Two hundred strings of silver and silk each were granted for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 州學教授阮希甫贈通直郎，防禦判官趙汝標、蘄春主簿寧時鳳、錄事參軍兼司戶杜諤俱贈承務郎，監蘄州都大監轄蘄口鎮倉庫嚴剛中贈承事郎。

translations.literal: University professor Ruan Xifu was posthumously made Regular Attendant; defense vice magistrate Zhao Rubiao, Qichun recorder Ning Shifeng, recording officer and revenue officer Du E were all posthumously made Gentlemen for Attending to Affairs; Qizhou chief overseer of the Qikou town granary Yan Gangzhong was posthumously made Gentleman for Attending to Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: University professor Ruan Xifu was posthumously made Regular Attendant. Defense vice magistrate Zhao Rubiao, Qichun recorder Ning Shifeng, and recording and revenue officer Du E were all posthumously made Gentlemen for Attending to Affairs. Qizhou chief overseer of the Qikou granary Yan Gangzhong was posthumously made Gentleman for Attending to Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時統製官孫中，小將江士旺、陳興、曹全、兵卞，軍士李斌等皆鬥死。

translations.literal: At that time commander Sun Zhong, junior generals Jiang Shiwang, Chen Xing, Cao Quan, and Bing Bian, and soldier Li Bin all died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Sun Zhong, junior generals Jiang Shiwang, Chen Xing, Cao Quan, and Bing Bian, and soldier Li Bin all died fighting.

sentences.zh: 司理參軍趙與裕先率民兵百餘人奪關出外求援，僅以身免，而全家十六人皆沒。

translations.literal: Judicial officer Zhao Yuyu first led more than a hundred militia to seize the pass and go out seeking relief; he alone escaped, but sixteen members of his family all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial officer Zhao Yuyu first led more than a hundred militia to break out seeking relief. He alone escaped, but sixteen members of his family perished.

sentences.zh: 淳祐十二年，特封钜義烈顯節侯。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chunyou Ju was specially enfeoffed as Marquis of Righteous Fervor and Manifest Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Chunyou Ju was specially enfeoffed as Marquis of Righteous Fervor and Manifest Integrity.

sentences.zh: 黃州之陷，守臣何大節亦投江死焉。

translations.literal: When Huangzhou fell, defending official He Dajie also threw himself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangzhou fell, defending official He Dajie also threw himself into the river and died.
